+//! Read-only retention inventory of one committed Store database.
+//!
+//! This is deliberately not a GC producer or a deletion permit. Other slots,
+//! Node's independent object database and seal-to-root publication exclusion
+//! are outside this snapshot. The check consumer reports that scope explicitly.
+use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet, VecDeque};
+use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
+
+use anyhow::{Context, Result, ensure};
+use rusqlite::{Connection, types::ValueRef};
+use serde::Serialize;
+use shenko_types::{commit::CommitRef, ids::{EntityId, LedgerSeq}, object::{Digest, ObjectRef}};
+
+use crate::{ContentStore, Store};
+
+mod artifacts;
+mod carriers;
+mod closure;
+
+/// Finite audit budgets, independent of mutation/admission budgets. Exceeding
+/// one makes the report incomplete; it never rejects a business transaction.
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]
+pub struct RetentionLimits {
+    pub rows: u64,
+    pub row_bytes: u64,
+    pub json_bytes: u64,
+    pub read_bytes: u64,
+    pub references: usize,
+    pub depth: usize,
+}
+
+impl Default for RetentionLimits {
+    fn default() -> Self {
+        Self { rows: 1_000_000, row_bytes: 8 * 1024 * 1024,
+            json_bytes: 64 * 1024 * 1024, read_bytes: 8 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024,
+            references: 65_536, depth: 64 }
+    }
+}
+
+impl RetentionLimits {
+    fn validate(&self) -> Result<()> {
+        let max = Self::default();
+        ensure!(self.rows > 0 && self.rows <= max.rows
+            && self.row_bytes > 0 && self.row_bytes <= max.row_bytes
+            && self.json_bytes > 0 && self.json_bytes <= max.json_bytes
+            && self.read_bytes > 0 && self.read_bytes <= max.read_bytes
+            && self.references > 0 && self.references <= max.references
+            && self.depth > 0 && self.depth <= max.depth,
+            "retention audit limits must be positive and within the reader's finite maxima");
+        Ok(())
+    }
+}
+
+/// Provenance contains identities and hashes, never the original row payload,
+/// a historical locator, an account credential or a provider response.
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]
+#[serde(tag = "kind", rename_all = "snake_case")]
+pub enum RetentionOrigin {
+    Row { table: String, column: String, ordinal: u64, value_digest: Digest },
+    Object { digest: Digest },
+    Schema { table: String },
+}
+
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]
+pub struct RetentionReference {
+    pub digest: Digest,
+    /// Typed ObjectRefs are required CAS members. The storage classification
+    /// distinguishes local artifact locators from implementation identities
+    /// and Node-inline or manifest-assembled artifacts. No classification
+    /// authorizes fetching a historical locator.
+    pub object: Option<ObjectRef>,
+    /// Some normalized cognition columns retain a CAS member by digest even
+    /// before another carrier supplies its full ObjectRef. Other bare digests
+    /// can name external files or implementation identities.
+    pub required: bool,
+    pub storage: RetentionStorage,
+    pub origin: RetentionOrigin,
+}
+
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]
+#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
+pub enum RetentionStorage {
+    CasObject,
+    CasDigest,
+    CasArtifact,
+    OptionalDigest,
+    ExternalArtifact,
+    NodeInlineArtifact,
+    ManifestAssembledArtifact,
+}
+
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]
+pub struct RetentionGap {
+    pub kind: String,
+    pub origin: RetentionOrigin,
+    pub digest: Option<Digest>,
+}
+
+#[derive(Debug, Serialize)]
+pub struct RetainedTable {
+    pub name: String,
+    pub rows_read: u64,
+    /// The exact ordered SQL values seen by this snapshot, with type/length
+    /// framing. None means a bounded or unsupported row was omitted.
+    pub values_digest: Option<Digest>,
+}
+
+#[derive(Debug, Serialize)]
+pub struct RetainedObjectSnapshot {
+    pub schema_version: u32,
+    pub scope: String,
+    pub database: Option<PathBuf>,
+    pub cas_directory: PathBuf,
+    pub ledger_id: EntityId,
+    pub source_through: LedgerSeq,
+    pub retained_commit_watermarks: Vec<CommitRef>,
+    pub sqlite_schema_cookie: i64,
+    pub schema_digest: Digest,
+    pub limits: RetentionLimits,
+    pub rows_read: u64,
+    pub bytes_read: u64,
+    pub json_bytes_read: u64,
+    pub tables: Vec<RetainedTable>,
+    pub derived_projections: Vec<String>,
+    pub references: Vec<RetentionReference>,
+    pub verified_objects: BTreeSet<Digest>,
+    pub external_or_absent_digests: BTreeSet<Digest>,
+    pub gaps: Vec<RetentionGap>,
+    pub omitted_gap_count: u64,
+    /// Completeness concerns this database's supported reference carriers.
+    /// It does NOT attest all-slot coverage or a stable deletion epoch.
+    pub complete: bool,
+}
+
+struct Reader<'a> {
+    cas: &'a ContentStore,
+    report: RetainedObjectSnapshot,
+    queue: VecDeque<RetentionReference>,
+    expanded: BTreeSet<(Digest, closure::JsonReading)>,
+    measured: BTreeMap<Digest, u64>,
+    exhausted: bool,
+}
+
+impl Reader<'_> {
+    fn gap(&mut self, kind: &str, origin: RetentionOrigin, digest: Option<Digest>) {
+        self.report.complete = false;
+        if self.report.gaps.len() < 256 {
+            self.report.gaps.push(RetentionGap { kind: kind.into(), origin, digest });
+        } else {
+            self.report.omitted_gap_count += 1;
+        }
+    }
+
+    fn charge(&mut self, bytes: u64, origin: &RetentionOrigin) -> bool {
+        match self.report.bytes_read.checked_add(bytes) {
+            Some(total) if total <= self.report.limits.read_bytes => {
+                self.report.bytes_read = total;
+                true
+            }
+            _ => {
+                self.gap("read_budget_exceeded", origin.clone(), None);
+                self.exhausted = true;
+                false
+            }
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+impl Store {
+    /// One live handle's consistent, committed SQLite view. CAS verification
+    /// is read-only but has no cross-process deletion exclusion.
+    pub fn retained_object_snapshot(&self, limits: RetentionLimits) -> Result<RetainedObjectSnapshot> {
+        limits.validate()?;
+        let catalogue = current_catalogue()?;
+        let mut conn = self.ledger.conn.lock();
+        let tx = conn.transaction()?;
+        let report = read_snapshot(&tx, &self.cas, limits, &catalogue)?;
+        ensure!(report.ledger_id == self.ledger.ledger_id(), "retention snapshot ledger changed");
+        tx.commit()?;
+        Ok(report)
+    }
+
+    /// The CLI's zero-touch path: use the existing stable DB/WAL tuple reader,
+    /// not Store::open, migrations, bootstrap preparation or a writer takeover.
+    pub fn inspect_retained_objects(
+        database: &Path, cas_directory: &Path, limits: RetentionLimits,
+    ) -> Result<RetainedObjectSnapshot> {
+        limits.validate()?;
+        let catalogue = current_catalogue()?;
+        let cas = ContentStore::open_existing(cas_directory.to_path_buf())?;
+        let mut report = Self::inspect_database(database, |conn| {
+            read_snapshot(conn, &cas, limits.clone(), &catalogue)
+        })?;
+        report.database = Some(database.to_path_buf());
+        Ok(report)
+    }
+}
+
+#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
+struct TableLayout {
+    kind: String,
+    columns: Vec<(String, String, i64)>,
+}
+
+fn quoted(name: &str) -> String { format!("\"{}\"", name.replace('"', "\"\"")) }
+
+fn table_layouts(conn: &Connection) -> Result<BTreeMap<String, TableLayout>> {
+    let mut query = conn.prepare("SELECT name,type FROM pragma_table_list WHERE schema='main' AND name NOT LIKE 'sqlite_%' ORDER BY name")?;
+    let mut rows = query.query([])?;
+    let mut tables = BTreeMap::new();
+    while let Some(row) = rows.next()? {
+        ensure!(tables.len() < 512, "retention schema exceeds the table budget");
+        let name: String = row.get(0)?;
+        let kind: String = row.get(1)?;
+        ensure!(name.len() <= 256, "retention table name exceeds its budget");
+        let mut columns = conn.prepare(&format!("PRAGMA main.table_xinfo({})", quoted(&name)))?;
+        let mut column_rows = columns.query([])?;
+        let mut fields = Vec::new();
+        while let Some(column) = column_rows.next()? {
+            ensure!(fields.len() < 256, "retention schema exceeds the column budget");
+            let field: String = column.get(1)?;
+            let declared: String = column.get(2)?;
+            ensure!(field.len() <= 256 && declared.len() <= 256, "retention column metadata exceeds its budget");
+            fields.push((field, declared.to_uppercase(), column.get(6)?));
+        }
+        // Additive migrations can leave an equivalent column in another
+        // physical position. Names/types/hidden semantics, not creation order,
+        // define the supported carrier layout.
+        fields.sort();
+        tables.insert(name, TableLayout { kind, columns: fields });
+    }
+    Ok(tables)
+}
+
+fn current_catalogue() -> Result<BTreeMap<String, TableLayout>> {
+    let conn = Connection::open_in_memory()?;
+    crate::store::initialize_schema(&conn)?;
+    table_layouts(&conn)
+}
+
+fn frame(hash: &mut blake3::Hasher, tag: &[u8], bytes: &[u8]) {
+    hash.update(tag);
+    hash.update(&(bytes.len() as u64).to_le_bytes());
+    hash.update(bytes);
+}
+
+fn schema_digest(conn: &Connection) -> Result<Digest> {
+    let mut query = conn.prepare("SELECT type,name,tbl_name,sql FROM main.sqlite_schema ORDER BY type,name")?;
+    let mut rows = query.query([])?;
+    let mut hash = blake3::Hasher::new();
+    let mut bytes = 0u64;
+    while let Some(row) = rows.next()? {
+        for index in 0..4 {
+            match row.get_ref(index)? {
+                ValueRef::Null => frame(&mut hash, b"null", &[]),
+                ValueRef::Text(text) => {
+                    bytes = bytes.checked_add(text.len() as u64).context("schema length overflow")?;
+                    ensure!(bytes <= 8 * 1024 * 1024, "retention schema exceeds its byte budget");
+                    frame(&mut hash, b"text", text);
+                }
+                _ => anyhow::bail!("invalid SQLite schema carrier"),
+            }
+        }
+    }
+    Ok(Digest(format!("blake3:{}", hash.finalize().to_hex())))
+}
+
+fn read_snapshot(
+    conn: &Connection, cas: &ContentStore, limits: RetentionLimits,
+    catalogue: &BTreeMap<String, TableLayout>,
+) -> Result<RetainedObjectSnapshot> {
+    let encoding: String = conn.pragma_query_value(None, "encoding", |row| row.get(0))?;
+    ensure!(encoding == "UTF-8", "retention audit does not support this database text encoding");
+    let ledger: String = conn.query_row("SELECT ledger_id FROM ledger_identity WHERE singleton=1", [], |row| row.get(0))?;
+    let through: u64 = conn.query_row("SELECT COALESCE(MAX(seq),0) FROM commit_log", [], |row| row.get(0))?;
+    let mut watermarks = conn.prepare("SELECT ledger_id,MAX(seq) FROM commit_log GROUP BY ledger_id ORDER BY ledger_id")?;
+    let mut rows = watermarks.query([])?;
+    let mut retained_commit_watermarks = Vec::new();
+    while let Some(row) = rows.next()? {
+        ensure!(retained_commit_watermarks.len() < 65_536, "retention commit origins exceed their budget");
+        let id: String = row.get(0)?;
+        retained_commit_watermarks.push(CommitRef::new(id.parse()?, LedgerSeq(row.get(1)?)));
+    }
+    drop(rows);
+    drop(watermarks);
+    let layouts = table_layouts(conn)?;
+    let mut reader = Reader {
+        cas,
+        report: RetainedObjectSnapshot {
+            schema_version: 1, scope: "single_committed_database".into(), database: None,
+            cas_directory: cas.base().to_path_buf(), ledger_id: ledger.parse()?,
+            source_through: LedgerSeq(through), retained_commit_watermarks,
+            sqlite_schema_cookie: conn.pragma_query_value(None, "schema_version", |row| row.get(0))?,
+            schema_digest: schema_digest(conn)?, limits, rows_read: 0, bytes_read: 0, json_bytes_read: 0,
+            tables: Vec::new(), derived_projections: Vec::new(),
+            references: Vec::new(), verified_objects: BTreeSet::new(),
+            external_or_absent_digests: BTreeSet::new(), gaps: Vec::new(), omitted_gap_count: 0,
+            complete: true,
+        },
+        queue: VecDeque::new(), expanded: BTreeSet::new(), measured: BTreeMap::new(), exhausted: false,
+    };
+    for (name, layout) in &layouts {
+        let origin = RetentionOrigin::Schema { table: name.clone() };
+        if catalogue.get(name) != Some(layout) {
+            reader.gap("unsupported_table_layout", origin, None);
+            continue;
+        }
+        if layout.kind != "table" {
+            // Only known rebuildable projections are excluded, and their
+            // names stay visible rather than silently disappearing.
+            reader.report.derived_projections.push(name.clone());
+            continue;
+        }
+        if reader.exhausted {
+            reader.gap("table_not_scanned_after_budget", origin, None);
+            continue;
+        }
+        read_table(conn, name, layout, &mut reader)?;
+    }
+    for (name, layout) in catalogue {
+        if layout.kind == "table" && !layouts.contains_key(name) {
+            reader.gap("missing_supported_table", RetentionOrigin::Schema { table: name.clone() }, None);
+        }
+    }
+    reader.expand_closure()?;
+    Ok(reader.report)
+}
+
+fn read_table(conn: &Connection, name: &str, layout: &TableLayout, reader: &mut Reader<'_>) -> Result<()> {
+    let columns: Vec<_> = layout.columns.iter().map(|(name, _, _)| quoted(name)).collect();
+    // octet_length(column) uses SQLite's length metadata before loading large
+    // text/BLOB bodies. The entire row is refused before any body is selected.
+    let size = columns.iter().map(|column| format!("COALESCE(octet_length({column}),0)"))
+        .collect::<Vec<_>>().join("+");
+    let values = columns.iter().map(|column| format!("CASE WHEN ({size})<=?1 THEN {column} END"))
+        .collect::<Vec<_>>().join(",");
+    let mut query = conn.prepare(&format!("SELECT ({size}),{values} FROM main.{}", quoted(name)))?;
+    let mut rows = query.query([reader.report.limits.row_bytes])?;
+    let mut count = 0;
+    let mut hash = blake3::Hasher::new();
+    let mut complete = true;
+    while let Some(row) = rows.next()? {
+        let origin = RetentionOrigin::Schema { table: name.to_owned() };
+        if reader.exhausted {
+            reader.gap("table_not_scanned_after_budget", origin, None);
+            complete = false;
+            break;
+        }
+        if reader.report.rows_read >= reader.report.limits.rows {
+            reader.gap("row_budget_exceeded", origin, None);
+            reader.exhausted = true;
+            complete = false;
+            break;
+        }
+        count += 1;
+        reader.report.rows_read += 1;
+        let size: u64 = row.get(0)?;
+        if size > reader.report.limits.row_bytes {
+            reader.gap("row_size_exceeded", origin, None);
+            complete = false;
+            continue;
+        }
+        if !reader.charge(size, &origin) { complete = false; break; }
+        for (index, (column, _, _)) in layout.columns.iter().enumerate() {
+            frame(&mut hash, b"column", column.as_bytes());
+            let value = row.get_ref(index + 1)?;
+            match value {
+                ValueRef::Null => frame(&mut hash, b"null", &[]),
+                ValueRef::Integer(number) => frame(&mut hash, b"integer", &number.to_le_bytes()),
+                ValueRef::Real(number) => frame(&mut hash, b"real", &number.to_bits().to_le_bytes()),
+                ValueRef::Text(bytes) | ValueRef::Blob(bytes) => {
+                    let is_blob = matches!(value, ValueRef::Blob(_));
+                    frame(&mut hash, if is_blob { b"blob" } else { b"text" }, bytes);
+                    let origin = RetentionOrigin::Row { table: name.into(), column: column.clone(),
+                        ordinal: count, value_digest: Digest::blake3(bytes) };
+                    if is_blob {
+                        if name == "context_window_derivatives" && column == "bytes" {
+                            // Embedded derivatives are data, not CAS pointers.
+                            // Their declared JSON form can still retain typed refs.
+                            let media = layout.columns.iter().position(|(name, _, _)| name == "media_type")
+                                .context("derivative media type missing")?;
+                            let media: String = row.get(media + 1)?;
+                            if closure::is_json(&media) { reader.json(bytes, &origin, true, 0, None); }
+                        } else {
+                            reader.gap("unsupported_blob_carrier", origin, None);
+                        }
+                    } else if carriers::required_digest(name, column) {
+                        reader.required_digest(bytes, &origin);
+                    } else if name == "memory_intents" && column == "content_ref" {
+                        reader.memory_locator(bytes, &origin);
+                    } else {
+                        reader.json(bytes, &origin, carriers::required_json(name, column), 0, None);
+                    }
+                }
+            }
+        }
+        frame(&mut hash, b"row_end", &[]);
+    }
+    reader.report.tables.push(RetainedTable { name: name.into(), rows_read: count,
+        values_digest: complete.then(|| Digest(format!("blake3:{}", hash.finalize().to_hex()))) });
+    Ok(())
+}"},{"sha":"d923ee9cc7169c5f0290573e3b236a4622311ca4","filename":"crates/shenko-store/src/retained_objects/artifacts.rs","status":"added","additions":164,"deletions":0,"changes":164,"blob_url":"https://github.com/cyjin-yl/shenko/blob/41d785ae8f968a3e81cd632223cadb356c44a224/crates%2Fshenko-store%2Fsrc%2Fretained_objects%2Fartifacts.rs","raw_url":"https://github.com/cyjin-yl/shenko/raw/41d785ae8f968a3e81cd632223cadb356c44a224/crates%2Fshenko-store%2Fsrc%2Fretained_objects%2Fartifacts.rs","contents_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/cyjin-yl/shenko/contents/crates%2Fshenko-store%2Fsrc%2Fretained_objects%2Fartifacts.rs?ref=41d785ae8f968a3e81cd632223cadb356c44a224","patch":"@@ -0,0 +1,164 @@
+//! Persisted artifact storage shapes, not executable admission. ToolArtifactRef
+//! is owned by shenko-wasm; this reader only interprets its storage description
+//! and follows the real manifest ObjectRef, without depending on that runtime.
+use serde_json::{Map, Value};
+
+use super::{Reader, RetentionOrigin, RetentionReference, RetentionStorage};
+use super::closure::{digest, is_json, object_reference, short_text};
+
+pub(super) fn chunk_manifest_reference(object: &shenko_types::object::ObjectRef) -> bool {
+    // Exact current CasToolContentStore::seal_bytes contract. Other storage
+    // adapters need a reader of their own; a JSON MIME type is insufficient.
+    is_json(&object.media_type)
+        && object.store_namespace == "wasm-tool-artifact"
+        && object.codec.name == "wasm-tool-artifact" && object.codec.major == 1
+        && object.codec.digest == shenko_types::object::Digest::blake3(b"wasm-tool-artifact")
+}
+
+/// The exact portable suffix produced by ContentStore, without allocating
+/// path components or opening any part of the historical path.
+fn cas_locator(locator: &str) -> Option<(&str, &str, &str)> {
+    let mut parts = locator.strip_prefix("file://")?.rsplit('/');
+    let hex = parts.next()?;
+    let shard = parts.next()?;
+    let parent = parts.next()?;
+    (hex.len() == 64 && hex.bytes().all(|byte| byte.is_ascii_digit() || (b'a'..=b'f').contains(&byte))
+        && shard.len() == 2 && parent.len() == 2).then_some((parent, shard, hex))
+}
+
+fn tool_shape(map: &Map<String, Value>) -> bool {
+    map.keys().all(|key| matches!(key.as_str(),
+        "kind" | "digest" | "bytes" | "media_type" | "store_namespace" | "sha256" | "chunk_manifest"))
+        && map.get("bytes").and_then(Value::as_u64).is_some()
+        && short_text(map, "media_type").is_some()
+        && short_text(map, "store_namespace").is_some()
+        && map.get("sha256").is_none_or(|value| value.is_null() || value.as_str().is_some())
+}
+
+/// This namespace's JSON objects are the current schema-1 chunk manifests.
+/// A syntactically valid JSON scalar cannot silently stand in for its edges.
+pub(super) fn readable_chunk_manifest(value: &Value) -> bool {
+    let Some(map) = value.as_object() else { return false; };
+    let Some(objects) = map.get("objects").and_then(Value::as_array) else { return false; };
+    map.keys().all(|key| matches!(key.as_str(),
+        "schema" | "artifact_digest" | "bytes" | "chunks" | "objects" | "sha256"))
+        && map.get("schema").and_then(Value::as_u64) == Some(1)
+        && map.get("artifact_digest").and_then(Value::as_str).and_then(digest).is_some()
+        && map.get("bytes").and_then(Value::as_u64).is_some()
+        && map.get("chunks").and_then(Value::as_u64) == Some(objects.len() as u64)
+        && objects.iter().all(|value| value.as_object().and_then(object_reference).is_some())
+        && map.get("sha256").is_none_or(|value| value.is_null() || value.as_str().is_some())
+}
+
+impl Reader<'_> {
+    pub(super) fn memory_locator(&mut self, bytes: &[u8], origin: &RetentionOrigin) {
+        if let Ok(locator) = std::str::from_utf8(bytes)
+            && let Some((parent, shard, hex)) = cas_locator(locator)
+            && parent == &hex[..2] && shard == &hex[2..4]
+        {
+            self.reference(RetentionReference {
+                digest: shenko_types::object::Digest(format!("blake3:{hex}")), object: None,
+                required: true, storage: RetentionStorage::CasArtifact, origin: origin.clone(),
+            });
+        } else {
+            // Historical memory may have only this String, without the newer
+            // full memory_intent_bindings ObjectRef. Do not silently drop it.
+            self.gap("unclassified_memory_content_locator", origin.clone(), None);
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// Return whether this map is an artifact/source descriptor, so it is not
+    /// also misread as an ObjectRef just because it has namespace and digest.
+    pub(super) fn artifact(&mut self, map: &Map<String, Value>, origin: &RetentionOrigin) -> bool {
+        if !map.contains_key("codec") && map.contains_key("kind")
+            && map.contains_key("store_namespace") && map.contains_key("digest")
+        {
+            self.tool_artifact(map, origin);
+            return true;
+        }
+        if map.contains_key("digest") && map.contains_key("locator")
+            && !["codec", "bytes", "media_type", "store_namespace"].iter().any(|key| map.contains_key(*key))
+        {
+            self.located_artifact(map, origin);
+            return true;
+        }
+        false
+    }
+
+    fn tool_artifact(&mut self, map: &Map<String, Value>, origin: &RetentionOrigin) {
+        let Some(identity) = map.get("digest").and_then(Value::as_str).and_then(digest) else {
+            self.gap("invalid_tool_artifact_digest", origin.clone(), None);
+            return;
+        };
+        let storage = match map.get("kind").and_then(Value::as_str) {
+            Some("content_store") => {
+                let manifest = map.get("chunk_manifest").and_then(Value::as_object).and_then(object_reference);
+                if manifest.as_ref().is_none_or(|object| !chunk_manifest_reference(object)) {
+                    self.gap("invalid_tool_chunk_manifest_reference", origin.clone(), Some(identity.clone()));
+                }
+                RetentionStorage::ManifestAssembledArtifact
+            }
+            Some("node_inline") => {
+                if map.get("chunk_manifest").is_some_and(|value| !value.is_null()) {
+                    self.gap("unexpected_inline_artifact_manifest", origin.clone(), Some(identity.clone()));
+                }
+                RetentionStorage::NodeInlineArtifact
+            }
+            _ => {
+                self.gap("unsupported_tool_artifact_storage", origin.clone(), Some(identity.clone()));
+                RetentionStorage::OptionalDigest
+            }
+        };
+        if !tool_shape(map) {
+            self.gap("invalid_tool_artifact_descriptor", origin.clone(), Some(identity.clone()));
+        }
+        // The whole-module digest is an identity, not a promised local object.
+        // The caller still descends into the actual chunk_manifest reference.
+        self.reference(RetentionReference {
+            digest: identity, object: None, required: false, storage, origin: origin.clone(),
+        });
+    }
+
+    fn located_artifact(&mut self, map: &Map<String, Value>, origin: &RetentionOrigin) {
+        let Some(identity) = map.get("digest").and_then(Value::as_str).and_then(digest) else {
+            self.gap("invalid_artifact_digest", origin.clone(), None);
+            return;
+        };
+        // SourceRef shares digest/locator with ArtifactRef but permits null.
+        // Full Task/Operation rows separately decode their non-null ArtifactRef.
+        let (storage, required) = match map.get("locator") {
+            Some(Value::String(locator)) => self.artifact_location(locator, &identity, origin),
+            Some(Value::Null) => (RetentionStorage::OptionalDigest, false),
+            _ => {
+                self.gap("invalid_artifact_locator", origin.clone(), Some(identity.clone()));
+                (RetentionStorage::OptionalDigest, false)
+            }
+        };
+        self.reference(RetentionReference {
+            digest: identity, object: None, required, storage, origin: origin.clone(),
+        });
+    }
+
+    fn artifact_location(
+        &mut self, locator: &str, identity: &shenko_types::object::Digest, origin: &RetentionOrigin,
+    ) -> (RetentionStorage, bool) {
+        if locator.starts_with("file://") {
+            if let Some((parent, shard, hex)) = cas_locator(locator) {
+                if hex == identity.hex() && parent == &hex[..2] && shard == &hex[2..4] {
+                    return (RetentionStorage::CasArtifact, true);
+                }
+                self.gap("artifact_locator_digest_disagrees", origin.clone(), Some(identity.clone()));
+                return (RetentionStorage::OptionalDigest, false);
+            }
+            return (RetentionStorage::ExternalArtifact, false);
+        }
+        if ["builtin:", "native:", "channel:", "http://", "https://", "provider://"]
+            .iter().any(|prefix| locator.starts_with(prefix))
+        {
+            return (RetentionStorage::ExternalArtifact, false);
+        }
+        // No location is read, normalized into a new authority or guessed.
+        self.gap("unclassified_artifact_location", origin.clone(), Some(identity.clone()));
+        (RetentionStorage::OptionalDigest, false)
+    }
+}"},{"sha":"8fb75225cb7649903a055207dbee6e94d4a5164d","filename":"crates/shenko-store/src/retained_objects/carriers.rs","status":"added","additions":91,"deletions":0,"changes":91,"blob_url":"https://github.com/cyjin-yl/shenko/blob/41d785ae8f968a3e81cd632223cadb356c44a224/crates%2Fshenko-store%2Fsrc%2Fretained_objects%2Fcarriers.rs","raw_url":"https://github.com/cyjin-yl/shenko/raw/41d785ae8f968a3e81cd632223cadb356c44a224/crates%2Fshenko-store%2Fsrc%2Fretained_objects%2Fcarriers.rs","contents_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/cyjin-yl/shenko/contents/crates%2Fshenko-store%2Fsrc%2Fretained_objects%2Fcarriers.rs?ref=41d785ae8f968a3e81cd632223cadb356c44a224","patch":"@@ -0,0 +1,91 @@
+//! Current column contracts. A `_ref` spelling alone is not a storage type:
+//! quota scope and historical memory locators are strings, while research
+//! object columns and committed decision columns contain complete ObjectRefs.
+use serde::de::DeserializeOwned;
+use serde_json::Value;
+use shenko_types::{authority::CommitAdmission, commit::CommitRef};
+
+use super::RetentionOrigin;
+
+pub(super) fn object_column(table: &str, column: &str) -> bool {
+    matches!((table, column),
+        ("research_epochs", "constraints_ref" | "budget_ref" | "effects_ref" | "environment_ref" | "brief_ref")
+        | ("research_candidates", "artifact_ref" | "environment_ref")
+        | ("subject_intents" | "subject_obligations" | "subject_attention_policies", "decision_ref")
+        | ("subject_request_attempts", "input_plan_ref")
+        | ("control_prepared_transitions", "transition_ref")
+        | ("cognition_contents", "object_json")
+        | ("recovery_sources", "data"))
+}
+
+pub(super) fn required_json(table: &str, column: &str) -> bool {
+    object_column(table, column)
+        || (column == "data" && !matches!(table, "raw_sessions" | "session_events" | "content_stream_units"))
+        || column.ends_with("_json")
+        || matches!((table, column),
+            ("identity_profiles", "profile") | ("context_windows", "body")
+            | ("cognition_baselines", "row_values")
+            | ("control_prepared_transitions", "admission" | "result_commit")
+            | ("subject_intents", "payload") | ("subject_attention_policies", "sources")
+            | ("channel_runtime_facts", "detail")
+            | ("research_epochs", "reset_receipt")
+            | ("intervention_bank_entries", "source_refs")
+            | ("intervention_reminders", "provenance" | "bank_entry_ids")
+            | ("retention_tombstones", "effect_record")
+            | ("content_streams", "opened_commit_ref" | "closed_commit_ref")
+            | ("media_streams", "open_commit_ref")
+            | ("media_stream_ends" | "media_segment_revisions" | "media_recordings"
+                | "media_recording_controls" | "media_priority_inputs", "admitted_commit_ref"))
+}
+
+pub(super) fn required_digest(table: &str, column: &str) -> bool {
+    matches!((table, column),
+        ("cognition_contents", "digest")
+        | ("cognition_attitudes", "digest" | "supersedes_content")
+        | ("cognition_legacy_content", "content_digest")
+        | ("cognitive_root_nodes" | "cognitive_root_requests", "content_digest"))
+}
+
+fn readable<T: DeserializeOwned>(value: &Value) -> bool {
+    T::deserialize(value).is_ok()
+}
+
+fn version_one<T: DeserializeOwned>(value: &Value) -> bool {
+    value.get("schema_version").and_then(Value::as_u64) == Some(1) && readable::<T>(value)
+}
+
+/// These root-bearing bookkeeping rows are not arbitrary raw events. Decode
+/// their current shape without invoking admission/recovery or rewriting a row.
+/// The generic walker still retains every visible edge, even after a refusal.
+pub(super) fn readable_row(value: &Value, origin: &RetentionOrigin) -> bool {
+    let RetentionOrigin::Row { table, column, .. } = origin else { return true; };
+    if object_column(table, column) {
+        return value.as_object().and_then(super::closure::object_reference).is_some();
+    }
+    match (table.as_str(), column.as_str()) {
+        ("control_prepared_transitions", "admission") => version_one::<CommitAdmission>(value),
+        ("control_prepared_transitions", "result_commit") => readable::<CommitRef>(value),
+        ("native_evidence_materializations", "data") =>
+            version_one::<crate::native_evidence::EvidenceMaterialization>(value),
+        ("native_evidence_deliveries", "data") =>
+            version_one::<crate::native_evidence_delivery::NativeEvidenceDeliveryRecord>(value),
+        ("native_evidence_seal_debts", "data") =>
+            version_one::<crate::native_evidence::NativeEvidenceSealDebt>(value),
+        ("local_installation_provisioning", "data") =>
+            version_one::<crate::local_installation::LocalInstallationProvisioning>(value),
+        ("reconciliation_cases", "data") => readable::<shenko_types::evidence::ReconciliationCase>(value),
+        ("tasks", "data") => readable::<shenko_types::task::TaskRecord>(value),
+        ("operations", "data") => readable::<shenko_types::operation::OperationRecord>(value),
+        ("attempts", "data") => readable::<shenko_types::operation::AttemptRecord>(value),
+        ("evidence_receipts", "data") => readable::<shenko_types::evidence::EvidenceReceipt>(value),
+        ("control_materializations", "data") => {
+            version_one::<CommitAdmission>(&value["admission"])
+                && readable::<CommitRef>(&value["committed_at"])
+                && value.get("logical_result").is_none_or(readable::<CommitRef>)
+                && value.get("transition_ref").is_none_or(|reference|
+                    reference.as_object().and_then(super::closure::object_reference).is_some())
+        }
+        ("cognition_baselines", "row_values") => readable::<Vec<(String, Option<String>)>>(value),
+        _ => true,
+    }
+}"},{"sha":"c3870c04ee143b228209383954f90b5e0e7d404b","filename":"crates/shenko-store/src/retained_objects/closure.rs","status":"added","additions":267,"deletions":0,"changes":267,"blob_url":"https://github.com/cyjin-yl/shenko/blob/41d785ae8f968a3e81cd632223cadb356c44a224/crates%2Fshenko-store%2Fsrc%2Fretained_objects%2Fclosure.rs","raw_url":"https://github.com/cyjin-yl/shenko/raw/41d785ae8f968a3e81cd632223cadb356c44a224/crates%2Fshenko-store%2Fsrc%2Fretained_objects%2Fclosure.rs","contents_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/cyjin-yl/shenko/contents/crates%2Fshenko-store%2Fsrc%2Fretained_objects%2Fclosure.rs?ref=41d785ae8f968a3e81cd632223cadb356c44a224","patch":"@@ -0,0 +1,267 @@
+//! Conservative retention references, not replication or execution authority.
+//! JSON-encoded row cells are followed, opaque CAS payloads are not interpreted.
+use std::io::Read;
+
+use anyhow::Result;
+use serde_json::{Map, Value};
+use shenko_types::object::{Digest, ObjectRef, SchemaRef};
+
+use super::{Reader, RetentionOrigin, RetentionReference, RetentionStorage};
+
+/// Equal bytes do not establish equal interpretations. In particular, a
+/// generic JSON walk must not satisfy the later tool-manifest shape reader.
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)]
+pub(super) enum JsonReading {
+    Generic,
+    ToolChunkManifest,
+}
+
+pub(super) fn is_json(media_type: &str) -> bool {
+    media_type == "application/json" || media_type.ends_with("+json")
+}
+
+pub(super) fn digest(text: &str) -> Option<Digest> {
+    let digest = Digest(text.into());
+    digest.canonical_blake3_hex().map(|_| digest.clone())
+}
+
+pub(super) fn short_text(map: &Map<String, Value>, key: &str) -> Option<String> {
+    let text = map.get(key)?.as_str()?;
+    (text.len() <= 1024).then(|| text.to_owned())
+}
+
+pub(super) fn object_reference(map: &Map<String, Value>) -> Option<ObjectRef> {
+    let codec = map.get("codec")?.as_object()?;
+    map.get("locator")?.as_str()?;
+    Some(ObjectRef {
+        digest: digest(map.get("digest")?.as_str()?)?,
+        bytes: map.get("bytes")?.as_u64()?,
+        media_type: short_text(map, "media_type")?,
+        store_namespace: short_text(map, "store_namespace")?,
+        // A historical locator is neither a read capability nor report data.
+        locator: String::new(),
+        codec: SchemaRef {
+            name: short_text(codec, "name")?,
+            major: u32::try_from(codec.get("major")?.as_u64()?).ok()?,
+            digest: digest(codec.get("digest")?.as_str()?)?,
+        },
+    })
+}
+
+impl Reader<'_> {
+    pub(super) fn required_digest(&mut self, bytes: &[u8], origin: &RetentionOrigin) {
+        if let Some(digest) = std::str::from_utf8(bytes).ok().and_then(digest) {
+            self.reference(RetentionReference {
+                digest, object: None, required: true, storage: RetentionStorage::CasDigest, origin: origin.clone(),
+            });
+        } else {
+            self.gap("invalid_required_digest", origin.clone(), None);
+        }
+    }
+
+    pub(super) fn reference(&mut self, reference: RetentionReference) {
+        if self.report.references.len() >= self.report.limits.references {
+            self.gap("reference_budget_exceeded", reference.origin, Some(reference.digest));
+            self.exhausted = true;
+            return;
+        }
+        self.queue.push_back(reference.clone());
+        self.report.references.push(reference);
+    }
+
+    pub(super) fn json(
+        &mut self, bytes: &[u8], origin: &RetentionOrigin, required: bool, depth: usize, object: Option<&ObjectRef>,
+    ) {
+        if self.exhausted { return; }
+        if depth > self.report.limits.depth {
+            self.gap("json_depth_exceeded", origin.clone(), None);
+            return;
+        }
+        // Parsing is independently bounded, including nested JSON strings.
+        let Some(total) = self.report.json_bytes_read.checked_add(bytes.len() as u64)
+            .filter(|total| *total <= self.report.limits.json_bytes) else {
+                self.gap("json_budget_exceeded", origin.clone(), None);
+                self.exhausted = true;
+                return;
+            };
+        self.report.json_bytes_read = total;
+        match serde_json::from_slice::<Value>(bytes) {
+            Ok(value) => {
+                if depth == 0 && !super::carriers::readable_row(&value, origin) {
+                    self.gap("invalid_column_carrier", origin.clone(), None);
+                }
+                if object.is_some_and(|object| object.store_namespace == "wasm-tool-artifact"
+                    && (!super::artifacts::chunk_manifest_reference(object)
+                        || !super::artifacts::readable_chunk_manifest(&value)))
+                {
+                    self.gap("unsupported_tool_chunk_manifest", origin.clone(), None);
+                }
+                self.value(&value, origin, depth);
+            }
+            Err(_) if required => self.gap("invalid_json_carrier", origin.clone(), None),
+            Err(_) => {
+                if let Ok(text) = std::str::from_utf8(bytes)
+                    && let Some(digest) = digest(text)
+                {
+                    self.reference(RetentionReference {
+                        digest, object: None, required: false, storage: RetentionStorage::OptionalDigest, origin: origin.clone(),
+                    });
+                }
+            }
+        }
+    }
+
+    fn value(&mut self, value: &Value, origin: &RetentionOrigin, depth: usize) {
+        if self.exhausted { return; }
+        if depth > self.report.limits.depth {
+            self.gap("json_depth_exceeded", origin.clone(), None);
+            return;
+        }
+        match value {
+            Value::Object(map) => {
+                if map.get("record_schema_version").is_some_and(|version| version.as_u64() != Some(1)) {
+                    // Current task/operation/attempt/E1 records all use version
+                    // one. Retain visible references, but do not claim that an
+                    // unknown record representation has a complete closure.
+                    self.gap("unsupported_record_schema_version", origin.clone(), None);
+                }
+                let artifact = self.artifact(map, origin);
+                // Missing namespace/codec is not permission to demote an
+                // ObjectRef-shaped carrier to a harmless optional digest.
+                let looks_typed = !artifact
+                    && ((map.contains_key("digest") && (map.contains_key("codec")
+                        || map.contains_key("store_namespace")
+                        || (map.contains_key("bytes") && map.contains_key("media_type"))))
+                        || (map.contains_key("store_namespace") && map.contains_key("codec")));
+                if looks_typed {
+                    if let Some(object) = object_reference(map) {
+                        self.reference(RetentionReference {
+                            digest: object.digest.clone(), object: Some(object), required: true,
+                            storage: RetentionStorage::CasObject, origin: origin.clone(),
+                        });
+                    } else {
+                        self.gap("invalid_object_reference", origin.clone(), None);
+                    }
+                    // Even a malformed reference may contain a retained digest.
+                    // Descend conservatively, without treating it as a valid proof.
+                }
+                for (key, nested) in map {
+                    // A valid ObjectRef's codec digest is a schema identity, not
+                    // an extra content edge. Other fields still support aliases.
+                    if (looks_typed && key == "codec") || (artifact && key == "digest") { continue; }
+                    self.value(nested, origin, depth + 1);
+                }
+            }
+            Value::Array(items) => {

+                    continue;
+                }

+                    continue;
+                }

+            let bytes = metadata.len();
+            if expected.is_some_and(|expected| expected != bytes) {
+                self.gap("object_length_disagrees", reference.origin, Some(reference.digest));
+                continue;
+            }
+            if json && bytes > self.report.limits.json_bytes.saturating_sub(self.report.json_bytes_read) {

+//! One bounded read refuses an oversized carrier, then a full read of the
+//! same committed original finds its embedded JSON reference without writes.
+use anyhow::{Context, Result};
+use shenko_store::{RetentionLimits, Store};
+use shenko_types::{ids::EntityId, store::{RawSession, RawSessionEvent, WriteBatch}};
+
+#[test]
+fn bounded_retention_refusal_keeps_the_original_rows_and_nested_cas_bytes() -> Result<()> {
+    let directory = tempfile::tempdir()?;
+    let database = directory.path().join("shenko.db");
+    let cas = directory.path().join("cas");
+    let store = Store::open(database.clone(), cas.clone())?;
+    let leaf = store.cas.seal_object(b"original retained output", "text/plain", "retention-test", "raw", 1)?.object;
+    let envelope = store.cas.seal_object(
+        &serde_json::to_vec(&serde_json::json!({"cell":{"type":"text","value":serde_json::to_string(&leaf)?}}))?,
+        "application/json", "retention-test", "row-carrier", 1,
+    )?.object;
+    let session = EntityId::new();
+    let event = EntityId::new();
+    let original = serde_json::to_string(&serde_json::json!({"evidence":&envelope}))?;
+    let mut batch = WriteBatch::new();
+    batch.raw_session_upserts.push(RawSession {
+        session_id: session, agent_id: EntityId::new(), started_at: "2026-11-16T00:00:00Z".into(), data: "{}".into(),
+    });
+    batch.session_event_upserts.push(RawSessionEvent {
+        event_id: event, session_id: session, seq: 0, event_type: "retention_observation".into(),
+        role: "system".into(), data: original.clone(),
+    });
+    store.commit(batch)?;
+    let through = store.current_commit_seq()?;
+    let objects = store.cas.object_digests()?;
+    let limits = RetentionLimits { row_bytes: 64, ..RetentionLimits::default() };
+    let refused = store.retained_object_snapshot(limits)?;
+    assert!(!refused.complete);
+    assert!(refused.gaps.iter().any(|gap| gap.kind == "row_size_exceeded"));
+    assert_eq!(store.current_commit_seq()?, through);
+    assert_eq!(store.session_events_range(session, 0, i64::MAX)?.first()
+        .context("original event was lost")?.data, original);
+    let paths = [database.clone(), database.with_extension("db-wal"), database.with_extension("db-shm")];
+    let before = paths.iter().map(|path| if path.exists() { std::fs::read(path).map(Some) } else { Ok(None) })
+        .collect::<std::io::Result<Vec<_>>>()?;
+    let report = Store::inspect_retained_objects(&database, &cas, RetentionLimits::default())?;
+    assert!(report.complete, "{:?}", report.gaps);
+    assert_eq!(report.ledger_id, store.ledger.ledger_id());
+    assert_eq!(report.source_through.0, through);
+    assert!(report.verified_objects.contains(&envelope.digest));
+    assert!(report.verified_objects.contains(&leaf.digest));
+    for (path, bytes) in paths.iter().zip(before) {
+        let after = if path.exists() { Some(std::fs::read(path)?) } else { None };
+        assert_eq!(after, bytes, "audit changed {}", path.display());
+    }
+    assert_eq!(store.cas.object_digests()?, objects);
+    assert_eq!(store.cas.read_object(&leaf.digest)?, b"original retained output");
+    assert_eq!(store.current_commit_seq()?, through);
+    Ok(())
+}"},{"sha":"9b9dd2c412fd7e871f7fe8378056d276a904399c","filename":"crates/shenko-update/src/build_tests.rs","status":"modified","additions":72,"deletions":14,"changes":86,"blob_url":"https://github.com/cyjin-yl/shenko/blob/41d785ae8f968a3e81cd632223cadb356c44a224/crates%2Fshenko-update%2Fsrc%2Fbuild_tests.rs","raw_url":"https://github.com/cyjin-yl/shenko/raw/41d785ae8f968a3e81cd632223cadb356c44a224/crates%2Fshenko-update%2Fsrc%2Fbuild_tests.rs","contents_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/cyjin-yl/shenko/contents/crates%2Fshenko-update%2Fsrc%2Fbuild_tests.rs?ref=41d785ae8f968a3e81cd632223cadb356c44a224","patch":"@@ -4,19 +4,52 @@

+//! Optional export of originals from existing update fixtures, never a replay.
+
+use std::fs::{self, File, OpenOptions};
+use std::io::{Read, Write};
+use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
+
+use anyhow::{Context, Result};
+use serde::Serialize;
+use shenko_types::ids::EntityId;
+use shenko_types::object::Digest;
+
+const FILE_LIMIT: u64 = 64 * 1024 * 1024;
+const EXPORT_LIMIT: u64 = 256 * 1024 * 1024;
+const ENTRY_LIMIT: usize = 4096;
+
+pub(crate) struct FixtureEvidence {
+    root: Option<PathBuf>,
+    entries: Vec<serde_json::Value>,
+    bytes: u64,
+    errors: Vec<String>,
+    finished: bool,
+    incomplete_installation: Option<PathBuf>,
+}
+
+impl FixtureEvidence {
+    pub(crate) fn new(name: &str) -> Result<Self> {
+        let configured = std::env::var_os("SHENKO_UPDATE_BUILD_EVIDENCE");
+        if let Some(root) = &configured {
+            anyhow::ensure!(!root.is_empty(), "SHENKO_UPDATE_BUILD_EVIDENCE is empty");
+        }
+        let root = configured.map(|root| PathBuf::from(root).join(format!("{name}-{}", EntityId::new())));
+        if let Some(root) = &root {
+            fs::create_dir_all(root.parent().context("evidence parent missing")?)?;
+            fs::create_dir(root)?;
+        }
+        let mut evidence = Self {
+            root, entries: Vec::new(), bytes: 0, errors: Vec::new(), finished: false,
+            incomplete_installation: None,
+        };
+        evidence.record("fixture-start", &serde_json::json!({
+            "fixture": name,
+            "source_revision_environment": std::env::var("SHENKO_SOURCE_REVISION").ok(),
+            "scope": "original observations from one existing fixture execution",
+            "source_snapshot_frozen": false,
+            "product_acceptance": false,
+        }));
+        Ok(evidence)
+    }
+
+    pub(crate) fn enabled(&self) -> bool { self.root.is_some() }
+
+    pub(crate) fn completed(&self) -> bool { self.finished && self.errors.is_empty() }
+
+    fn failure(&mut self, label: &str, error: anyhow::Error) {
+        let message = format!("update fixture evidence {label}: {error:#}");
+        eprintln!("{message}");
+        self.errors.push(message);
+    }
+
+    fn save(&mut self, label: &str, bytes: &[u8], original_path: Option<&Path>) -> Result<()> {
+        let Some(root) = &self.root else { return Ok(()); };
+        anyhow::ensure!(self.entries.len() < ENTRY_LIMIT, "evidence entry limit reached");
+        anyhow::ensure!(bytes.len() as u64 <= FILE_LIMIT, "evidence file limit reached");
+        let total = self.bytes.checked_add(bytes.len() as u64).context("evidence size overflow")?;
+        anyhow::ensure!(total <= EXPORT_LIMIT, "evidence export limit reached");
+        let name = format!("{:04}.blob", self.entries.len());
+        let mut file = OpenOptions::new().write(true).create_new(true).open(root.join(&name))?;
+        file.write_all(bytes)?;
+        file.sync_all()?;
+        self.bytes = total;
+        self.entries.push(serde_json::json!({
+            "file": name, "label": label, "original_path": original_path,
+            "bytes": bytes.len(), "digest": Digest::blake3(bytes),
+            "observed_at": chrono::Utc::now().to_rfc3339(),
+        }));
+        self.write_index()
+    }
+
+    fn write_index(&self) -> Result<()> {
+        let Some(root) = &self.root else { return Ok(()); };
+        let bytes = serde_json::to_vec_pretty(&serde_json::json!({
+            "schema_version": 1, "entries": self.entries, "errors": self.errors,
+            "fixture_completed": self.finished,
+            "incomplete_original_installation": self.incomplete_installation,
+            "source_snapshot_frozen": false,
+        }))?;
+        let pending = root.join("index.next.json");
+        let mut file = File::create(&pending)?;
+        file.write_all(&bytes)?;
+        file.sync_all()?;
+        drop(file);
+        fs::rename(pending, root.join("index.json"))?;
+        Ok(())
+    }
+
+    pub(crate) fn record<T: Serialize>(&mut self, label: &str, value: &T) {
+        if !self.enabled() { return; }
+        let result = serde_json::to_vec_pretty(value).map_err(anyhow::Error::from)
+            .and_then(|bytes| self.save(label, &bytes, None));
+        if let Err(error) = result { self.failure(label, error); }
+    }
+
+    pub(crate) fn file(&mut self, label: &str, path: &Path) {
+        if !self.enabled() { return; }
+        let result = (|| {
+            let metadata = fs::symlink_metadata(path)?;
+            anyhow::ensure!(metadata.file_type().is_file(), "original is not a regular file: {}", path.display());
+            anyhow::ensure!(metadata.len() <= FILE_LIMIT, "original file exceeds export limit: {}", path.display());
+            let mut bytes = Vec::new();
+            File::open(path)?.take(FILE_LIMIT + 1).read_to_end(&mut bytes)?;
+            self.save(label, &bytes, Some(path))
+        })();
+        if let Err(error) = result { self.failure(label, error); }
+    }
+
+    pub(crate) fn tree(&mut self, label: &str, path: &Path) {
+        if !self.enabled() { return; }
+        let result = (|| {
+            anyhow::ensure!(fs::symlink_metadata(path)?.file_type().is_dir(), "original tree is not a directory");
+            let mut pending = vec![path.to_path_buf()];
+            let mut visited = 0_usize;
+            while let Some(directory) = pending.pop() {
+                for entry in fs::read_dir(directory)? {
+                    visited += 1;
+                    anyhow::ensure!(visited <= ENTRY_LIMIT, "original tree entry limit reached");
+                    let entry = entry?;
+                    let kind = entry.file_type()?;
+                    if kind.is_dir() { pending.push(entry.path()); }
+                    else if kind.is_file() { self.file(label, &entry.path()); }
+                    else { anyhow::bail!("original tree has a non-regular entry: {}", entry.path().display()); }
+                }
+            }
+            Ok(())
+        })();
+        if let Err(error) = result { self.failure(label, error); }
+    }
+
+    pub(crate) fn owned_file(&mut self, label: &str, path: &Path, owner: &Path) {
+        if !self.enabled() { return; }
+        let result = (|| {
+            let path = fs::canonicalize(path)?;
+            anyhow::ensure!(path.starts_with(fs::canonicalize(owner)?), "artifact is outside its owned fixture");
+            self.file(label, &path);
+            Ok(())
+        })();
+        if let Err(error) = result { self.failure(label, error); }
+    }
+
+    /// Only fixture-owned installations are watched. On early failure their
+    /// current bytes are retained with coherence explicitly unasserted. The
+    /// normal path exports after all original Store handles have been dropped.
+    #[cfg(unix)]
+    pub(crate) fn watch_installation(&mut self, path: &Path) {
+        self.incomplete_installation = Some(path.to_path_buf());
+    }
+
+    #[cfg(unix)]
+    pub(crate) fn closed_installation(&mut self, path: &Path) {
+        self.record("installation-handles-dropped", &serde_json::json!({ "original_path": path }));
+        self.tree("closed-original-installation", path);
+        self.incomplete_installation = None;
+    }
+
+    pub(crate) fn finish(&mut self) -> Result<()> {
+        if self.errors.is_empty() {
+            self.finished = true;
+            if let Err(error) = self.write_index() { self.failure("finish", error); }
+        }
+        anyhow::ensure!(self.errors.is_empty(), "{}", self.errors.join("\n"));
+        Ok(())
+    }
+}
+
+impl Drop for FixtureEvidence {
+    fn drop(&mut self) {
+        if !self.enabled() || self.completed() { return; }
+        if let Some(path) = self.incomplete_installation.take() {
+            self.record("incomplete-scope-exit", &serde_json::json!({
+                "original_path": path, "thread_panicking": std::thread::panicking(),
+                "database_snapshot_consistency": "not asserted",
+                "cleanup_or_process_join": "not inferred from scope exit",
+            }));
+            self.tree("incomplete-original-installation-bytes", &path);
+        }
+        if let Err(error) = self.write_index() { self.failure("incomplete-index", error); }
+        eprintln!("update fixture did not complete its evidence export; retained originals: {:?}; errors: {:?}",
+            self.root, self.errors);
+    }
+}"},{"sha":"fea54b37f3669cafe2e39711ebd1610b33e2dd9e","filename":"docs/IMPLEMENTATION_DOCS_MAP.md","status":"modified","additions":1,"deletions":0,"changes":1,"blob_url":"https://github.com/cyjin-yl/shenko/blob/41d785ae8f968a3e81cd632223cadb356c44a224/docs%2FIMPLEMENTATION_DOCS_MAP.md","raw_url":"https://github.com/cyjin-yl/shenko/raw/41d785ae8f968a3e81cd632223cadb356c44a224/docs%2FIMPLEMENTATION_DOCS_MAP.md","contents_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/cyjin-yl/shenko/contents/docs%2FIMPLEMENTATION_DOCS_MAP.md?ref=41d785ae8f968a3e81cd632223cadb356c44a224","patch":"@@ -163,6 +163,7 @@

+# Installation write permits: implementation plan
+
+This is a source audit and a proposed implementation boundary, not an installed
+permit or an acceptance result. The audit is bound to
+`c9db3aa8e315a1ea320d67584fdbff1129312762` (tree
+`39f65e771eb299d2c342d61ceb2dc8528f028276`). The existing seat admission/outcome
+increment has nine distinct scenarios and the [PTY receipt increment](pty-write-flush-receipts.md)
+has five; this plan adds none. It does not reduce the
+[remote-seat contract](../specs/remote-seats.md) or
+[completion scope](../governance/COMPLETION.md).
+
+## Boundary to implement together
+
+The useful boundary is cooperative seat writing within one verified physical
+installation, including every local mutation that can invalidate its task,
+lease, incarnation or selected software generation. A process-local seat mutex,
+an extra check before a transport await, or a lock held only by the caller cannot
+establish that boundary.
+
+Two non-cloneable capabilities are needed:
+
+- An installation mutation permit orders cooperating live mutations and final
+  slot cutovers. It grants neither primary authority nor permission to send.
+- A physical seat-write permit is obtained only by the Current admission path,
+  after its actual final T1 checks. It names the original installation, selected
+  slot, task invocation, seat/incarnation, lease/epoch/capability and exact input.
+  Prepared or Learned recovery cannot manufacture it from an Armed row.
+
+The low-level coordination primitive must be shared by Store, Node, update and
+the physical owner without a Store/Node dependency cycle. Its stable inode is
+separate from every SQLite file and from the root directory already locked by
+`RuntimeOwner`. Validate the directory and named inode on admission. An advisory
+lock is coordination, not a new source of installation identity or selection.
+Initial enrollment, existing installation admission and same-installation slot
+copies must use the same verified physical domain; an archive or foreign
+manifest cannot supply it. Unsupported backends must refuse this capability,
+not return an unlocked guard.
+
+## Final admission order
+
+1. Construct and seal the original proposal. Complete provider preparation and
+   quorum/network work without holding an installation permit.
+2. Acquire the installation permit before any Node reservation or Store/import
+   transaction. A cancelled waiter cannot later become a sender.
+3. Acquire the actual source reservation and perform the existing final checks
+   and T1 transaction with a borrowed permit.
+4. Finish the Store transaction and drop the Node/source guard. Only the Current
+   path may move the original physical permit into the actual writer.
+5. Keep that permit until the original local write/flush completes or the
+   original local writer is proven unable to issue more writes.
+6. Release physical ownership before starting a new E1/settlement admission.
+
+The proposal is not re-evaluated on a lock conflict. Existing chosen debt,
+fixed IDs/results, exact predecessor checks and original receipts remain.
+`AuthorityReservation::Drop` must retain its existing nonblocking
+`action_unmaterialized` behavior and release source guards before its permit.
+
+Explicit borrowed-permit APIs are necessary for nested calls. Proposed shapes
+include `open_under`, `with_mutation_under`, `reserve_*_under` and
+`import_*_under`; these are design names, not existing APIs. Do not infer
+reentrancy from a thread-local flag or open a second lock descriptor in a nested
+call. Holding a Node transaction while waiting for a physical writer would
+reverse the required order.
+
+## Live callsite coverage
+
+| Current source surface | Required integration |
+| --- | --- |
+| `Store::open`, schema initialization, `Ledger::new` | Obtain the domain permit before persistent PRAGMAs, migrations and identity writes. `channel::migrate_publication_targets` at the end of open must borrow it rather than reacquire. |
+| `Ledger::with_mutation` | Cover every ordinary commit, seat/task/control mutation, generic `WriteBatch`, canonical application and factual settlement while retaining the original writer-failure latch. |
+| `authority.rs` reservation entry points | Move domain acquisition before `provider.acquire`; preserve network preparation outside the final permit. The current provider acquires a Node transaction and then reads Store. |
+| `RuntimeAuthority`, `runtime_branches`, installed Node RPC/control paths | Use the same domain before Node initialization/reservation and authority-changing transactions; nested request handling borrows the original permit. |
+| `seat.rs` | Include registration, relocation, retirement, incarnation, lease acquire/end, questions and decisions. Covering only `arm_seat_answer_decision` leaves invalidators outside exclusion. |
+| `cognition/import.rs` | Coordinate the existing import gate and live file/Git/row publication, including task/seat semantic units. Downloaded archive content does not grant a physical permit. |
+| `recovery_sources.rs` | Include the actual live metadata INSERT currently outside `with_mutation`; private staging databases are not installed writers. |
+| `slots.rs` | Cover consistent backup, copied ledger identity change, manifest publication and final pointer publication. Do not copy the physical lock into a slot. The currently unused public READ_WRITE `open_slot_db` is an API bypass to remove or constrain. |
+| `handoff.rs` | Apply one final-cutover protocol to `activate_inner`, `rollback_inner` and `finish_committed_handoff`, including candidate CAS, source mirror, head fence and pointer. |
+| CLI/runtime openers | Start/bootstrap, branch, tools, context, update and other live Store openers must carry the same installed domain. A legacy constructor cannot silently bypass it for the same installed database. |
+| `SeatRuntime` and adapters | Move the original physical permit to the actual writer. A plain `SeatWriteFence` data value is not an ownership capability. |
+
+Bare live SQLite/file mutation paths must be audited before calling this set
+complete. Merely adding a new optional API while old installed paths remain
+unguarded is not this increment.
+
+The concrete entry points above are in
+[`store.rs`](../../crates/shenko-store/src/store.rs),
+[`ledger.rs`](../../crates/shenko-store/src/ledger.rs),
+[`authority.rs`](../../crates/shenko-store/src/authority.rs),
+[`runtime_authority.rs`](../../bin/shenko/src/runtime_authority.rs),
+[`runtime_branches.rs`](../../bin/shenko/src/runtime_branches.rs),
+[`seat.rs`](../../crates/shenko-store/src/seat.rs),
+[`cognition/import.rs`](../../crates/shenko-store/src/cognition/import.rs),
+[`recovery_sources.rs`](../../crates/shenko-store/src/recovery_sources.rs),
+[`slots.rs`](../../crates/shenko-update/src/slots.rs) and
+[`handoff.rs`](../../crates/shenko-update/src/handoff.rs).
+
+## Current selection and historical facts
+
+Fresh physical admission must verify the actual selector/head projection,
+sealed route identity and physical root/slot paths under the permit. The checks
+in `context_windows.rs::verify_selected_context_slot` provide useful principles,
+not a complete active-generation resolver:
+
+- Match SQL selector projections with their original body, generation and head.
+- Validate the immutable route's bytes, digest, schema, subject and origin.
+- Do not require route epoch/revision equality: a legitimate takeover can
+  retain an older sealed route. Future values remain invalid.
+- Refuse the exact unresolved source Handoff revision, even if its old
+  head/selector/route still agree before the mirror is repaired.
+- Treat `current-slot` as a convenience pointer, never selection authority.
+
+After asynchronous drain/primary checks and local preparation, final cutover
+must acquire one permit, re-read both slots, perform the candidate CAS, mirror
+it, fence the original head and publish the pointer. Recovery performs the
+corresponding original repair under the same permit. Old handles must fail fresh
+physical admission after a cutover, even if an old lease still looks Current in
+their retained database.
+
+Historical E1, learned materialization and original reconciliation still
+participate in domain serialization, but cannot be required to become the fresh
+selected writer. A blanket stale-slot rejection would discard legitimate late
+facts. Neither historical admission nor an update maintenance operation yields
+a send permit.
+
+## Physical ownership remains adapter-specific
+
+### SSH PTY
+
+Move the permit into the original queued `Command` and then `Pump.active`.
+Keep it across channel-window/rekey queues and the actual channel-scoped flush
+receipt. Cancellation closes the original `OwnedStream` before releasing it.
+Keep original input/error retention, Queued-to-NotSent and Writing-to-Unknown;
+late success cannot replace Unknown. This is a local write boundary, not remote
+acceptance or withdrawal of bytes already transmitted.
+
+### Managed stdio
+
+The existing `ManagedProcess::write_frame` holds the original stdin mutex across
+`write_all` and `flush`, and retains a cancelled frame's identity/Unknown latch.
+It does not spawn another writer in this repository. The permit belongs inside
+that physical writer ownership, not in its outer adapter caller. The pinned
+platform implementation of Tokio `ChildStdin` must still be verified before
+asserting that cancellation leaves no background writer. The
+[Tokio 1.54.1 public implementation](https://docs.rs/tokio/1.54.1/src/tokio/process/mod.rs.html)
+delegates to the platform implementation; that delegation alone is not the
+missing proof.
+
+Plan the final JSONL bytes, including newline, before T1. The current managed
+answer path parses a planned JSON payload and serializes it again in the writer;
+submit/interrupt allocate protocol IDs after the outer native T1. Preserve old
+readable facts, but do not treat their payload digest as a newly proven exact
+wire digest. A typed plan/seal/seat-aware arm path is required. The expected
+frozen seat ID must also reach `SeatRespondRequest` and its final check.
+
+### tmux through OpenSSH or a local shell
+
+Current `SshExecutor` cancellation requests process-group termination and relies
+on `kill_on_drop`; it does not establish a joined physical writer before the
+caller disappears. Parent-process crashes do not run Rust Drop.
+
+Direct inheritance of an extra permit FD into OpenSSH is not a valid solution:
+the [official portable client source](https://github.com/openssh/openssh-portable/blob/master/ssh.c)
+calls `closefrom(STDERR_FILENO + 1)` at the start of `main`. This audit read that
+official source, not the exact binary installed by a particular runner. A
+supervisor holding the FD is also incomplete if its own crash releases the lock
+while its child can continue writing.
+
+Before claiming this adapter is covered, either connect its original guarded
+commands to an actually owned native SSH transport, preserving authentication
+and complete results, or implement an execution owner with durable in-flight
+facts and a verifiable stop boundary across its own crash. The local shell path
+needs its own equivalent proof. Unknown never becomes an automatic resend. If
+an adapter cannot provide the capability, a request for it must be refused,
+not silently routed through the original unguarded path.
+
+## Native tmux prerequisite: actual call audit
+
+This section proposes the next transport prerequisite. It does not install it,
+make the OpenSSH path continuously fenced, or change an existing capability.
+The source binding is the same `c9db3aa8e315a1ea320d67584fdbff1129312762` above.
+
+### Existing paths are not interchangeable
+
+[`TmuxSeatAdapter::remote`](../../crates/shenko-exec-ssh/src/seat/tmux.rs)
+constructs [`TmuxSeat::remote`](../../crates/shenko-exec-ssh/src/ssh_exec.rs),
+which uses [`SshExecutor::over_ssh`](../../crates/shenko-exec-ssh/src/executor.rs).
+It always uses real SSH, including a loopback endpoint. Each command starts
+an independent OpenSSH process. It does not load user/system ssh_config or
+reuse ControlMaster, so preserving unspecified ProxyCommand configuration is
+not a requirement of this existing API.
+
+| Property | Existing OpenSSH tmux path | Existing installed native transport |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Target | `SshTarget` host, port and account; validated before process spawn | The same endpoint fields in a complete `SshBinding`, plus a `NativeInstallationSeal` for installed use |
+| Private identity | Explicit key path, explicitly enabled ambient agent, or both; default private identities are disabled | File opener reads one exact absolute file, checks permissions/type/size and matches the installed public key; no passphrase source or agent discovery |
+| Agent support | `use_agent=true` requires the caller's `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`; OpenSSH selects from that authorized agent | Protocol API accepts an explicit public identity and `Signer`; the installed file adapter does not provide an agent implementation |

+and [`native_transport/stream.rs`](../../crates/shenko-exec-ssh/src/native_transport/stream.rs).
+An OpenSSH configuration that native transport cannot represent must remain
+on its explicitly chosen compatibility path or be refused when native mode is
+requested. Silently selecting a different key, trust source or transport is not
+a migration.

+### Runtime entry and identity gaps

+The audited repository has no production caller of

+That method explicitly skips `host != "local"`, because the location record
+does not carry an SSH binding. Adding only a native constructor would therefore
+leave the new behavior unused by Start.
+

+attachment path:

+  Multiple remote servers can legitimately have the same pane ID. The new

+  the raw pane ID used by tmux on that server.

+  remote pane must be selected by exact identity before attachment, not by the
+  server's list order. The Store already checks the active `(host, pane_id)`

+
+Actual configured native SSH is already wired:
+[`runtime_start.rs`](../../bin/shenko/src/runtime_start.rs) receives `ssh_targets`,

+and [`SshTaskRunner`](../../crates/shenko-exec-ssh/src/task_runner.rs): target
+selection is evidence, T1 precedes authentication, and retry queries the
+original frozen operation. The map is currently private to that handler;
+the seat generation does not have the same installed registry.
+
+### Proposed smallest live-wired native mode
+
+Implement one explicit installed-native tmux attachment and answer path as a
+coherent prerequisite, without claiming installation exclusion. Keep existing
+local and OpenSSH constructors and their original records readable. The
+proposed scope is:

+The native mode must consume the already owned

+Its full guarded command and limits must be planned before the relevant T1;
+the existing tmux text-only plan is not a proof that a subsequently rebuilt
+remote shell command was frozen. Actual command completion remains an

+## Boundedness and exclusions
+
+An indefinitely blocked frame cannot hold the whole installation hostage.
+The original owner needs an explicit bounded write/stop policy and cancellation
+outside the database gate. It cannot require a task-cancel transaction to obtain
+the same permit before the physical writer learns it must stop. Time elapsed
+does not itself prove a local writer stopped or a remote action ended.
+
+This design does not authorize a primary, fence arbitrary older binaries or
+external SQL writers, stop independent human input, prove remote execution has
+ended, or provide physical exactly-once. It does not automatically cover model

+# Native SSH command cleanup observations
+
+The existing single-command native SSH transport closed its original owned
+stream and then used `timeout(..., handle).await.is_ok()` to record local session
+end. That boolean correctly distinguished a bounded wait from an observed end,
+but discarded an error actually returned by the original session handle.
+
+[`NativeSshSession::execute`](../../crates/shenko-exec-ssh/src/native_transport/mod.rs)
+now preserves three separate facts in `NativeCommandObservation`:
+
+- `local_stream_closed` records that the original synchronous `OwnedStream`
+  close completed before the cleanup wait. Later underlying I/O polls are
+  refused by that stream; this is not a claim that the remote process stopped.
+- `session_end_observed` records a completed original session handle, including
+  an error completion. A cleanup deadline leaves this false.
+- `session_error` retains the Debug rendering of that handle's actual error.
+  It is absent when no such error was observed, including a timed-out wait;
+  absence alone does not prove a successful join.
+
+These are additive fields in the existing observation. They do not replace the
+command's original interruption, binary stdout/stderr, exec acceptance, channel
+closure, or real remote exit status. In particular, a remote exit 255 remains a
+remote status, and a command deadline remains uncertain even if the local
+session subsequently ends. The cleanup bound and its validation are unchanged.
+Cancelling the whole caller before it returns still leaves no completed
+observation; the existing durable T1/recovery path must preserve that uncertainty
+and cannot resend the original command.
+
+## Actual consumers
+
+This is an existing execution path, not a new installer or unused permit API:
+
+- [`ssh.exec`](../../crates/shenko-exec-ssh/src/native.rs) serializes the complete
+  observation into its original E1 payload. Its conclusive transport rules are
+  unchanged; an exit is not an application postcondition.
+- [`SshTaskRunner::record_observation`](../../crates/shenko-exec-ssh/src/task_runner.rs)
+  seals the complete native observation alongside the original helper receipt
+  and dispatch error. The installed `ssh.native` handler already consumes this
+  path. No legacy OpenSSH result or stored historical fact is rewritten.
+
+The stored error is specifically the result returned by the original russh
+handle. This increment does not claim that every earlier internal protocol
+error survives a later library shutdown error, or change the library's error
+precedence. It does not introduce a new remote effect, physical-write permit,
+trust source, credential choice, retry path or installed tmux capability.
+
+## Validation boundary
+
+The existing real authenticated SSH protocol journeys over bounded in-memory
+streams gain assertions for two already exercised paths: a completed 128 KiB
+duplex exchange with remote exit 255, and an accepted command that reaches its
+original deadline. In each, the server retains its original session until the
+client explicitly closes the owned stream. The new assertions require the
+actual returned local-close error and preserve all previous output, exit and
+uncertainty assertions. They do not fabricate a session result or add a second
+execution route.
+
+The two existing `ssh.exec` receipt projection checks also carry the new fields
+and assert that serialization preserves them without changing Complete versus
+Unknown. Thus four existing checks are amended, of which two perform real SSH
+protocol exchanges; no new test function or scenario matrix is added. The prior
+nine seat admission/outcome scenarios and five PTY write scenarios are unchanged.
+
+The current local environment has no `cargo`, `rustc` or `rustfmt`. Source review
+and `git diff --check` are the available checks for this increment; its Rust
+compilation and actual protocol assertions await CI. The full installation
+mutation/slot exclusion and explicit native tmux attachment remain separate
+work."},{"sha":"3b7f20b7f4390e7a3058e4e122d3dddb602f8e2d","filename":"docs/development/pty-write-flush-receipts.md","status":"modified","additions":59,"deletions":9,"changes":68,"blob_url":"https://github.com/cyjin-yl/shenko/blob/41d785ae8f968a3e81cd632223cadb356c44a224/docs%2Fdevelopment%2Fpty-write-flush-receipts.md","raw_url":"https://github.com/cyjin-yl/shenko/raw/41d785ae8f968a3e81cd632223cadb356c44a224/docs%2Fdevelopment%2Fpty-write-flush-receipts.md","contents_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/cyjin-yl/shenko/contents/docs%2Fdevelopment%2Fpty-write-flush-receipts.md?ref=41d785ae8f968a3e81cd632223cadb356c44a224","patch":"@@ -4,6 +4,10 @@ This increment connects the existing SSH PTY seat to an actual local transport
