+# Read-only Store retention inventory
+
+`shenko --data-dir <installation> check --retained-objects` reads one existing
+Store and its CAS, prints a bounded JSON inventory, and returns failure when
+that inventory has gaps. It enters before the ordinary `check` command opens
+a writer or prepares home state. The existing `check` behavior is unchanged
+when the option is absent.
+
+The command uses the existing stable main-database/WAL tuple inspector. It
+copies a finite, signature-checked tuple to a private temporary directory and
+lets SQLite read the committed view there. It does not migrate the original
+database, initialize its SHM, take over the writer, create an installation or
+repair a home. The temporary copy still needs disk proportional to the tuple;
+the new row/object limits below are not a claim that staging a large database
+uses constant disk space. A missing database or CAS directory is an error.
+
+An installation's `current-slot` pointer chooses the physical database for
+this command. It is only a selection hint: the output names the database and
+does not attest that it is the authoritative active generation. Initial,
+historical, candidate and staging sibling slots are outside that output.
+
+## Source and carrier scope
+
+`Store::retained_object_snapshot` reads a live handle in one read transaction.
+`Store::inspect_retained_objects` reads the same information through the
+private tuple inspector. Both bind the ledger identity, maximum physical
+commit sequence, retained per-ledger commit watermarks, SQLite schema cookie,
+schema digest and exact typed-value digests of the table rows read. The table
+digest includes column names, SQL types, lengths and row boundaries in the
+observed scan order. A skipped or oversized row prevents a complete table
+digest. The report contains source identities and hashes, not original row
+payloads, provider output, account credentials or historical locator values.
+
+The current additive Store schemas are initialized in a separate, empty
+in-memory connection to obtain the supported table catalogue. That operation
+does not open a Store writer or manufacture a source commit. The inventory
+reads every current base table, including local tables excluded from cognition
+replication. Known FTS projections and their shadow tables are derived and
+excluded; an unknown table, changed carrier layout, unsupported BLOB, invalid
+required JSON, unsupported record representation or exhausted budget makes
+the inventory explicitly incomplete. The scanner does not migrate a historical
+layout to make it look supported.
+
+The included local carriers cover prepared control transitions and physical
+materialization receipts; first and successor E1 seals; pending, blocked and
+applied delivery descriptors; seal debts and reconciliation cases; local home
+provisioning; cognitive root nodes and requests; and cognition baselines.
+The general raw-session/event and activation carriers retain completed build
+observations and their recovery closures. Ordinary task, operation, attempt,
+original evidence and receipt-conflict records are read in the same snapshot.
+
+Typed `ObjectRef` members are mandatory CAS objects. Known independent object
+columns, including research and decision references, must decode as complete
+objects: JSON `null`, arrays or missing reference fields cannot silently mean
+an empty closure. Local E1/delivery/home and canonical preparation/application
+records also decode their current root-bearing shapes. A malformed carrier
+still contributes every readable edge while making the inventory incomplete.
+The normalized cognition content-digest columns also require local bytes.
+
+`ArtifactRef` has only a digest and locator. A canonical CAS file locator's
+digest/shard suffix identifies required local bytes even when its historical
+installation prefix differs; that prefix is never read. Builtin, native,
+channel and declared external locations remain separately classified. An
+unclassified location or conflicting CAS suffix is a gap. `SourceRef` may
+also carry a digest with a null locator; it remains an optional digest, while
+typed Task/Operation decoding checks their non-null `ArtifactRef` contract.
+The historical `memory_intents.content_ref` string also requires its canonical
+CAS-suffix member; an unrecognized legacy locator is an explicit gap rather
+than an empty root set. Newer memory bindings additionally carry the complete
+ObjectRef and its JSON reading where applicable.
+
+The installed `ToolArtifactRef` storage descriptor is a different shape, with
+no ObjectRef codec. Its `content_store` form retains the real JSON chunk
+manifest and its ObjectRefs; the reassembled module digest is an identity,
+not a promise of a whole-module CAS file. Its `node_inline` form identifies
+Node's independent object database. Unsupported kinds, malformed descriptors
+or unsupported chunk manifests make the inventory incomplete. These storage
+readings do not invoke a tool or verify an installation's selection authority.
+The manifest edge must name the current Store adapter's namespace and codec.
+Generic JSON and tool-manifest expansion are cached as different readings of
+the same digest; seeing bytes through the former never bypasses the latter's
+shape check. Each additional read/parse consumes the same byte/JSON budgets,
+and every manifest edge still checks its own codec and declared size.
+
+Other canonical bare digests may name external executable files, Git content,
+schema identities or optional aliases; an absent bare digest is listed
+separately instead of being invented as a local object. The reader never
+follows a locator or retrieves a credential.
+
+Object bytes must have the declared length and digest. JSON-typed objects are
+walked recursively, including JSON embedded in strings by canonical
+`Cell::Text` and cognition baseline row values. This is conservative retention
+discovery, not validation of an admission, decoder, effect or peer claim.
+Opaque raw output, WASM and other non-JSON payloads do not acquire graph
+authority by resembling JSON. A digest seen first as opaque can still be
+expanded when a later typed JSON reference supplies that reading. Invalid
+required carriers and missing mandatory objects remain visible gaps; the
+reader does not substitute a new seal or discard their references.
+
+## Bounds and refusals
+
+Default maxima are one million rows, 8 MiB per selected row, 64 MiB of aggregate
+JSON input (including nested encoded JSON), 8 GiB of streamed SQL/CAS bytes,
+65,536 reference occurrences and JSON depth 64. Callers can lower these limits,
+not raise them. Schema inspection separately limits the number of tables,
+columns, metadata name lengths and schema text. Diagnostic details are capped
+at 256 entries while a counter records further gaps.
+
+The reader requires the Store's UTF-8 database encoding. SQL row bodies are
+selected only after `octet_length(column)` reports that their aggregate input
+fits the row bound. SQLite documents that text/BLOB column length metadata
+allows this check without loading the whole value
+([SQLite core functions](https://sqlite.org/lang_corefunc.html#octet_length)).
+CAS files are streamed in 64 KiB buffers, with a regular-file check, final
+digest verification and a one-byte overrun check; only bounded JSON bodies are
+retained for parsing. These are input/work bounds, not an assertion about every
+internal allocation of SQLite or a JSON value tree.
+
+`complete=true` means the supported reference carriers in this one committed
+database were enumerated and their mandatory local objects verified within
+these limits. It does not resolve a pending delivery, validate a malformed E1
+proof, acknowledge Unknown, authorize a worker, make an effect conclusive or
+prove a candidate executable. A report can retain the bytes of such unresolved
+facts without declaring their business outcome successful.
+Generic JSON discovery enumerates visible reference shapes; it does not
+establish that every application codec was semantically decoded or validated.
+
+## Verification scope
+
+This increment adds three bounded risk/recovery observations:
+
+1. The existing authenticated E1 journey observes its already-present interrupted
+   download as an incomplete mandatory root, then inventories the real first,
+   successor and acknowledgement history at source and receiver. The public
+   `check --retained-objects` path is exercised against that receiver. Original
+   receipt, two-effect, no-T2, replay and Unknown assertions remain intact.
+2. The existing prepare/reopen journey checks that both the raw build observation
+   and the candidate recovery closure retain the original build receipt and
+   outcome. This does not add a build qualification claim.
+3. One Store journey lowers the row bound, observes explicit refusal, then
+   inspects the same committed row and its nested JSON/CAS reference with the
+   normal bound. It checks unchanged original event text, DB/WAL/SHM bytes,
+   commit watermark and CAS inventory/content.
+
+These are three added retention observations, separate from the six frozen
+GC declaration windows. The candidate has static review only in the recovered
+workspace: Rust, Cargo and the documentation parser environment are absent.
+Compilation and these actual journeys remain pending integration CI.
+The later carrier-reader correction adds no scenario or injected corruption
+window. Its storage-shape review follows `types/object.rs`, the research and
+control/E1 row writers, `wasm/artifact.rs` and the real
+`tool_install::bind_artifact_to_recovery` carrier. It has no independent
+executed ToolArtifact/corruption validation claim.
+
+## Remaining deletion boundary
+
+This reader is not registered as `CasRootProducer`, and no runtime GC scheduler
+or reclamation path is added. A complete installation inventory must still
+cover every shared-CAS slot and all non-Store producers. Node control objects
+live in a separate object database; a queued Store descriptor does not pretend

+# Original observations from the existing update fixtures
+
+The optional `SHENKO_UPDATE_BUILD_EVIDENCE` sink retains observations from the existing Cargo build and prepare/reopen tests. The existing Rust CI test step now sets it to `.ci/evidence/update-build`; the already unconditional artifact upload includes that directory. The same step enables the separate `SHENKO_PTY_WRITE_EVIDENCE` sink. No test command, compiler option, timeout, ignore, baseline or gate changes.
+
+## Why the export is needed
+
+[CI 3e62](../evidence/ci-3e62c0e5-20261116/README.md) actually passed the existing build and PTY assertions. Its successful PTY diagnostics were captured by libtest, and its build/prepare fixtures deleted their temporary originals. The runner result is valid within that scope, but the missing raw receipts are unavailable for independent inspection. This change only retains the next actual execution; it cannot reconstruct that prior run.
+
+## Retained data
+
+Each update fixture creates a unique directory beneath the explicit sink. Its index records original paths, byte lengths, BLAKE3 digests and export observation times. Numbered `.blob` files preserve bytes; their index labels distinguish typed JSON observations, source inputs, compiled artifacts and copied CAS/installation files.
+
+- Each original `BuildOutcome` or `BuildError` is recorded immediately after its real invocation returns, before its existing assertions. The typed JSON includes the exact bounded byte arrays, EOF/truncation counts, actual exit and cleanup observations, Cargo metadata/version, source observations and refusal. No UTF-8 replacement is used for raw streams.
+- The existing A/B/C source files are copied before their original invocations. These are observations of fixture inputs, not a frozen source image or a reproducible-build claim. The actual selected artifact bytes are exported only from the fixture's owned directory. The original old/rebuilt executable runs keep their complete `CommandObservation`.
+- The existing successful and failed CAS seals retain their actual object references and immutable CAS files. The existing reopen assertions still verify the same original bytes.
+- The three existing prepare refusals retain their actual candidate bytes and returned errors. Their reopened raw session events and the successful prepare/reopen events remain original Store reads. On the normal path all fixture and reopened Store handles are dropped before the installation files are copied, then evidence completion must succeed before the existing cleanup removes the temporary installation.
+
+The export does not traverse Cargo target caches or unrelated temporary directories. A file is limited to 64 MiB, an export to 256 MiB and a traversed tree/index to 4,096 entries. Non-regular files and copy failures are reported. These are evidence-export bounds, not altered compiler output limits or product acceptance thresholds.
+
+## Failure semantics
+
+Writes happen while the original values are still available. Export errors are printed and retained; they cannot turn a successful fixture into an evidence pass. The original assertions and failure messages remain in place. On a successful test path, a failed export returns an error before deleting the original workspace or installation. Partial files and prior atomically published indexes remain available.
+
+An early-return or panic retains the already observed build outcomes. Incomplete Cargo workspaces are left at their original paths. For a watched, fixture-owned installation, scope-exit export retains the bytes it can read and explicitly marks database snapshot consistency and process cleanup as **unasserted**. Those incomplete bytes are not a consistent backup or a join receipt. An export never reruns the candidate, reopens a Store, seals replacement facts or claims an unobserved success.
+
+## Scope and validation
+
+This adds **zero behavioral windows**. The original five build windows and three existing refusal windows remain unchanged; the independent prepared-artifact window keeps their combined bound at nine. No original input, assertion, success condition, command, byte limit or duration changes. `test_evidence` is compiled only under `cfg(test)` and has no production API consumer.
+
+Local validation is limited to source review, preservation checks of the original assertions and invocation budgets, exact workflow comparison, and `git diff --check`. Cargo, rustc and rustfmt are unavailable in the current local environment. The exporter has not executed here; a subsequent exact-candidate CI must validate its compile and actual output. This does not prove the tested-self-modification loop, source freeze, full smoke policy, NapCat/coding-seat integration, migration/activation acceptance, or 7/30-day operation."},{"sha":"405f202a2583dd7373824b60c7c204a56d254b8f","filename":"docs/evidence/README.md","status":"modified","additions":2,"deletions":0,"changes":2,"blob_url":"https://github.com/cyjin-yl/shenko/blob/41d785ae8f968a3e81cd632223cadb356c44a224/docs%2Fevidence%2FREADME.md","raw_url":"https://github.com/cyjin-yl/shenko/raw/41d785ae8f968a3e81cd632223cadb356c44a224/docs%2Fevidence%2FREADME.md","contents_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/cyjin-yl/shenko/contents/docs%2Fevidence%2FREADME.md?ref=41d785ae8f968a3e81cd632223cadb356c44a224","patch":"@@ -2,6 +2,8 @@

This archive preserves that actual result and its limits; it adds no behavioral scenario and does not rerun product work.

+## What passing S2 build and PTY tests do and do not retain
+
+The successful test results include the actual Cargo rebuild/error, ambiguous-target, compiler-overflow, prepare/reopen, and PTY write/flush/cancel/channel-loss fixtures. The Cargo fixtures invoke the actual Cargo executable on temporary Rust 2024 projects. They do not use a fabricated compiler result. The PTY fixture exercises its original native SSH protocol peer and five existing windows; it is not an OpenSSH OS PTY or a complete coding-seat journey.

+- The Cargo fixtures check original streams and CAS reopen behavior, then delete their temporary workspaces and CAS in `Drop`. The prepare/reopen fixture also deletes its temporary installation after closing its Store. Those raw originals are absent from this run's artifact.
+
+Therefore this archive does not claim independent access to those missing successful-test originals. +#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Archive already observed CI originals; never execute or replay product work."""
+from pathlib import Path
+import datetime
+import gzip
+import hashlib
+import json
+import re
+import shutil
+import subprocess
+import zipfile
+
+ROOT = Path('/workspace/scratch/faaa3ccca531')
+SRC = ROOT / 'ci-3e62c0e5-43968540714'
+REPO = ROOT / 'shenko'
+DST = REPO / 'docs/evidence/ci-3e62c0e5-20261116'
+HEAD = '3e62c0e517a246872101cd1e61a694b2156bc919'
+
+def sha(data):
+    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
+
+def write_json(path, data):
+    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    path.write_text(json.dumps(data, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + '\n')
+
+def copy(source, target):
+    target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    shutil.copyfile(source, target)
+    assert source.read_bytes() == target.read_bytes()
+
+def compressed(source, target):
+    raw = source.read_bytes()
+    target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    target.write_bytes(gzip.compress(raw, mtime=0))
+    assert gzip.decompress(target.read_bytes()) == raw
+
+def unwrap(path):
+    obj = json.loads(path.read_text())
+    while isinstance(obj, dict) and 'structuredContent' in obj:
+        obj = obj['structuredContent']
+    if isinstance(obj, dict) and isinstance(obj.get('content'), str):
+        obj = json.loads(obj['content'])
+    return obj
+
+DST.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
+for source in sorted(SRC.glob('*.tool.json')):
+    compressed(source, DST / 'connector-originals' / (source.name + '.gz'))
+for source in sorted(SRC.glob('*.job.original.log')):
+    copy(source, DST / source.name)
+for source in sorted(SRC.glob('*.download-verification.json')):
+    copy(source, DST / source.name)
+for name in ['archive-transport-failure.json', 'clippy-derived-summary.json']:
+    copy(SRC / name, DST / name)
+
+mapping = {
+    'final-run.tool.json': 'run.api.json',
+    'jobs-final.tool.json': 'jobs.api.json',
+    'final-artifacts.tool.json': 'artifacts.api.json',
+    'actual-checkout.tool.json': 'actual-checkout.api.json',
+    'requested-head.tool.json': 'requested-head.api.json',
+}
+for source, target in mapping.items():
+    write_json(DST / target, unwrap(SRC / source))
+run = unwrap(SRC / 'final-run.tool.json')
+assert run['head_sha'] == HEAD and run['conclusion'] == 'failure'
+checkout = unwrap(SRC / 'actual-checkout.tool.json')
+head = unwrap(SRC / 'requested-head.tool.json')
+assert checkout['tree']['sha'] == head['tree']['sha']
+artifacts = unwrap(SRC / 'final-artifacts.tool.json')['artifacts']
+inventory = []
+for item in artifacts:
+    path = SRC / (item['name'] + '.original.zip')
+    raw = path.read_bytes()
+    assert len(raw) == item['size_in_bytes']
+    assert 'sha256:' + sha(raw) == item['digest']
+    copy(path, DST / path.name)
+    with zipfile.ZipFile(path) as archive:
+        assert archive.testzip() is None
+        members = [{'path': x.filename, 'bytes': x.file_size, 'crc32': f'{x.CRC:08x}',
+                    'sha256': sha(archive.read(x))} for x in archive.infolist()]
+    inventory.append({'artifact_id': item['id'], 'file': path.name, 'bytes': len(raw),
+                      'sha256': sha(raw), 'members': members, 'crc_ok': True})
+write_json(DST / 'artifact-inventory.derived.json', inventory)
+
+for name in ['workspace-test.log', 'workspace-check.log']:
+    copy(SRC / 'rust-evidence' / name, DST / name)
+copy(SRC / 'clippy-ratchet-evidence/clippy/ratchet.json', DST / 'clippy-ratchet.json')
+copy(SRC / 'clippy-ratchet-evidence/base.json', DST / 'clippy-base.json')
+copy(SRC / 'web-rebuild-evidence/comparison.json', DST / 'web-comparison.json')
+for path in sorted((SRC / 'rust-evidence/native-e1').rglob('*')):
+    if path.is_file():
+        copy(path, DST / 'native-e1' / path.relative_to(SRC / 'rust-evidence/native-e1'))
+
+test_log = (SRC / 'rust-evidence/workspace-test.log').read_text()
+pattern = r'test result: (ok|FAILED)\. (\d+) passed; (\d+) failed; (\d+) ignored; (\d+) measured; (\d+) filtered out.*'
+summaries = []
+for line in test_log.splitlines():
+    match = re.search(pattern, line)
+    if match:
+        summaries.append({'original_line': line, 'status': match[1],
+            **dict(zip(['passed', 'failed', 'ignored', 'measured', 'filtered_out'], map(int, match.groups()[1:])))})
+counts = {key: sum(row[key] for row in summaries) for key in ['passed', 'failed', 'ignored', 'measured', 'filtered_out']}
+assert len(summaries) == 152 and counts == dict(passed=1094, failed=0, ignored=11, measured=0, filtered_out=90)
+focus = ['original_native_e1_arrives_over_authenticated_ssh_without_t2_or_reexecution',
+    'original_pty_writes_observe_flush_cancel_errors_and_channel_loss',
+    'redirected_cargo_rebuild_keeps_the_actual_artifact_and_failed_attempt',
+    'two_real_matching_cargo_targets_are_refused_as_ambiguous',
+    'overflowing_real_compiler_output_is_stopped_and_never_an_artifact',
+    'prepare_keeps_its_build_observation_in_raw_history_and_the_recovery_closure']
+write_json(DST / 'test-summaries.derived.json', {'source': 'workspace-test.log', 'count': len(summaries),
+    'totals': counts, 'summaries': summaries,
+    'selected_original_result_lines': [line for line in test_log.splitlines() if any(name in line for name in focus)],
+    'raw_receipt_retention_gap': 'Successful PTY eprintln was libtest-captured; build and handoff temporary originals were deleted by their fixtures. These assertions passed, but their missing raw originals cannot be reconstructed from this run.'})
+
+nested = SRC / 'rust-evidence/native-e1/020-native-e1-originals.zip'
+with zipfile.ZipFile(nested) as archive:
+    assert archive.testzip() is None
+    original_inventory = json.loads(archive.read('inventory.json'))
+    for record in original_inventory:
+        raw = archive.read(record['member'])
+        assert len(raw) == record['bytes'] and sha(raw) == record['sha256']
+    manifest = json.loads(archive.read('manifest.json'))
+    sides = {}
+    text_count = 0
+    for side in manifest['stores']:
+        ledger = json.loads(archive.read(side + '/ledger-rows.json'))
+        for rows in ledger['tables'].values():
+            for row in rows:
+                for key, expected in row.get('text_sha256', {}).items():
+                    assert sha(row['values'][key].encode()) == expected
+                    text_count += 1
+        references = json.loads(archive.read(side + '/cas-references.json'))
+        sides[side] = {
+            'scope': ledger['scope'],
+            'row_counts': {key: len(value) for key, value in ledger['tables'].items()},
+            'branch_head_original_data': [json.loads(row['values']['data']) for row in ledger['tables']['subject_branch_heads']],
+            'reconciliation_original_data': [json.loads(row['values']['data']) for row in ledger['tables']['reconciliation_cases']],
+            'seal_debt_original_data': [json.loads(row['values']['data']) for row in ledger['tables']['native_evidence_seal_debts']],
+            'missing_references': [entry for entry in references['references'] if 'missing' in entry],
+            'excluded_digest_count': len(references['excluded_digests']),
+            'untyped_digest_count': len(references['untyped_digests']),
+        }
+    effects = archive.read('physical-effects.raw')
+    assert effects == b'effect\neffect\n'
+    validation = {
+        'source': 'native-e1/020-native-e1-originals.zip', 'bytes': nested.stat().st_size,
+        'sha256': sha(nested.read_bytes()), 'members': len(archive.infolist()), 'crc_ok': True,
+        'original_inventory_entries_verified': len(original_inventory), 'original_text_hashes_verified': text_count,
+        'blake3_recomputed_locally': False,
+        'blake3_limit': 'The local Python environment has no blake3 module; SHA-256/length/CRC and original text digests are independently checked. This is not a new product execution.',
+        'original_manifest': manifest, 'physical_effects_hex': effects.hex(), 'physical_effect_lines': 2,
+        'stores': sides,
+    }
+    (DST / 'native-e1/nested-manifest.original.json').write_bytes(archive.read('manifest.json'))
+write_json(DST / 'native-e1-originals-validation.derived.json', validation)
+
+paths = [
+    '.github/workflows/ci.yml', 'scripts/ci/clippy_ratchet.py',
+    'crates/shenko-exec-ssh/src/seat/ssh_pty/pump.rs',
+    'crates/shenko-exec-ssh/src/native_transport/tests/pty_write.rs',
+    'crates/shenko-update/src/build.rs', 'crates/shenko-update/src/build_tests.rs',
+    'crates/shenko-update/src/handoff_tests.rs',
+    'crates/shenko-store/src/native_evidence_successor.rs',
+    'bin/shenko/tests/native_evidence_delivery.rs',
+]
+blobs = []
+for path in paths:
+    result = subprocess.run(['git', 'show', HEAD + ':' + path], cwd=REPO, capture_output=True, check=True)
+    data = result.stdout
+    blob = subprocess.check_output(['git', 'rev-parse', HEAD + ':' + path], cwd=REPO, text=True).strip()
+    target = DST / 'source-blobs' / (blob + '.blob')
+    target.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
+    target.write_bytes(data)
+    assert hashlib.sha1(b'blob ' + str(len(data)).encode() + b'\0' + data).hexdigest() == blob
+    blobs.append({'path': path, 'git_blob': blob, 'bytes': len(data), 'sha256': sha(data),
+                  'retained_as': str(target.relative_to(DST))})
+write_json(DST / 'source-blobs.json', {'source_head': HEAD, 'actual_checkout': checkout['sha'],
+    'tree': head['tree']['sha'], 'files': blobs})
+print(json.dumps({'archive': str(DST), 'artifact_members': sum(len(x['members']) for x in inventory),

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Retain selected original fixture rows and CAS bytes, never the installation.
+
+This is a read-only evidence export, not a byte-for-byte SQLite backup. Node
+databases, owner-token tables, SSH configuration and keys are never selected.
+Only typed references in the listed fixture namespaces can disclose CAS bytes.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import base64
+from collections import deque
+import hashlib
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+import re
+import sqlite3
+import zipfile
+
+TABLES = (
+    "subject_genesis", "subject_branch_heads", "subject_steps", "tasks",
+    "task_results", "operations", "attempts", "evidence_receipts",
+    "evidence_receipt_conflicts", "evidence_key_conflicts",
+    "reconciliation_cases", "subject_intents", "inbox_events", "session_events",
+    "subject_event_dispositions", "control_prepared_transitions",
+    "control_materializations", "native_evidence_materializations",
+    "native_evidence_seal_debts", "native_evidence_deliveries",
+    "context_windows", "context_window_scopes", "cognition_origins", "commit_log",
+)
+REQUIRED_TABLES = {
+    "commit_log", "tasks", "operations", "attempts", "evidence_receipts",
+    "control_materializations", "native_evidence_materializations",
+}
+NAMESPACES = {
+    "test", "commit-authority", "input_plans", "model_outcomes",
+    "native-e1-fixture",
+}
+SECRET_FIELDS = {
+    "password", "passwd", "secret", "private_key", "api_key", "access_token",
+    "refresh_token", "authorization", "cookie", "token", "token_hash",
+    "bearer_token", "credential", "credentials", "client_secret",
+    "owner_control_token",
+}
+DIGEST = re.compile(r"blake3:([0-9a-f]{64})\Z")
+MAX_OBJECTS = 4096
+MAX_BYTES = 64 * 1024 * 1024
+
+
+def encoded(value):
+    return (json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n").encode()
+
+
+def sha256(raw):
+    return hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()
+
+
+def secret_field(value):
+    if isinstance(value, dict):
+        for key, item in value.items():
+            if key.lower() in SECRET_FIELDS and item not in (None, "", [], {}):
+                return key
+            if found := secret_field(item):
+                return found
+    elif isinstance(value, list):
+        for item in value:
+            if found := secret_field(item):
+                return found
+    elif isinstance(value, str) and value.lstrip()[:1] in ("{", "["):
+        try:
+            return secret_field(json.loads(value))
+        except (json.JSONDecodeError, RecursionError):
+            pass
+    return None
+
+
+def references(value, via):
+    if isinstance(value, dict):
+        if (
+            isinstance(value.get("digest"), str)
+            and DIGEST.fullmatch(value["digest"])
+            and isinstance(value.get("bytes"), int)
+            and value["bytes"] >= 0
+            and all(key in value for key in ("media_type", "store_namespace", "codec"))
+        ):
+            yield value, via
+            return
+        for key, item in value.items():
+            yield from references(item, f"{via}/{key}")
+    elif isinstance(value, list):
+        for index, item in enumerate(value):
+            yield from references(item, f"{via}/{index}")
+    elif isinstance(value, str) and value.lstrip()[:1] in ("{", "["):
+        # RowTransition's Cell::Text preserves row JSON as an encoded string.
+        # Follow its typed references without rewriting the original string,
+        # and retain the extra decode step in the evidence traversal route.
+        try:
+            nested = json.loads(value)
+        except json.JSONDecodeError:
+            return
+        yield from references(nested, f"{via}/<json>")
+
+
+def cell(value):
+    if isinstance(value, bytes):
+        return {
+            "sqlite_type": "blob", "base64": base64.b64encode(value).decode(),
+            "bytes": len(value), "sha256": sha256(value),
+        }
+    return value
+
+
+def snapshot(data_dir):
+    database = data_dir / "shenko.db"
+    if not database.exists():
+        return None, [], {"reason": "Store database was not created before failure"}
+    if database.is_symlink():
+        raise ValueError("fixture database is a symlink")
+    roots = []
+    result = {
+        "schema_version": 1, "source_database": str(database),
+        "scope": "selected original row values from one read transaction; not a SQLite backup",
+        "text_values": "original strings, including data JSON text, are not decoded or rewritten",
+        "blob_values": "lossless base64 with byte length and SHA256",
+        "tables": {}, "missing_tables": [], "omitted_tables": [], "excluded_rows": [],
+        "omitted_columns": {"commit_log": "only ledger_id, seq, created_at, entity_count"},
+    }
+    with sqlite3.connect(database.resolve().as_uri() + "?mode=ro", uri=True) as connection:
+        connection.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
+        connection.execute("BEGIN")
+        available = {
+            row[0] for row in connection.execute(
+                "SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table'"
+            )
+        }
+        result["omitted_tables"] = sorted(available.difference(TABLES))
+        for table in TABLES:
+            if table not in available:
+                result["missing_tables"].append(table)
+                continue
+            query = (
+                "SELECT ledger_id,seq,created_at,entity_count FROM commit_log ORDER BY seq,ledger_id"
+                if table == "commit_log" else f'SELECT rowid AS "__rowid__",* FROM "{table}" ORDER BY rowid'
+            )
+            kept = []
+            for row in connection.execute(query):
+                raw = dict(row)
+                if field := secret_field(raw):
+                    result["excluded_rows"].append({
+                        "table": table, "rowid": raw.get("__rowid__"),
+                        "reason": f"credential-bearing field {field}; original not disclosed",
+                    })
+                    continue
+                values = {key: cell(value) for key, value in raw.items()}
+                kept.append({
+                    "values": values,
+                    "text_sha256": {
+                        key: sha256(value.encode("utf-8"))
+                        for key, value in raw.items() if isinstance(value, str)
+                    },
+                })
+                for key, value in raw.items():
+                    if isinstance(value, str):
+                        try:
+                            roots.extend(references(json.loads(value), f"{table}/{raw.get('__rowid__')}/{key}"))
+                        except json.JSONDecodeError:
+                            pass
+            result["tables"][table] = kept
+        connection.rollback()
+    return result, roots, None
+
+
+def closure(data_dir, roots):
+    pending = deque(roots)
+    seen = set()
+    expanded = set()
+    retained = {}
+    excluded = {}
+    records = []
+    total = 0
+    cas = data_dir / "cas"
+    while pending:
+        reference, via = pending.popleft()
+        signature = json.dumps(reference, sort_keys=True)
+        if signature in seen:
+            continue
+        seen.add(signature)
+        if len(seen) > MAX_OBJECTS * 4:
+            raise ValueError("fixture reference budget exceeded")
+        digest = DIGEST.fullmatch(reference["digest"]).group(1)
+        record = {"reference": reference, "via": via}
+        records.append(record)
+        if reference["store_namespace"] not in NAMESPACES:
+            record["excluded"] = "namespace not in fixture disclosure allowlist"
+            excluded[digest] = record["excluded"]
+            continue
+        path = cas / digest[:2] / digest[2:4] / digest
+        if path.is_symlink() or not path.resolve().is_relative_to(cas.resolve()):
+            record["excluded"] = "CAS reference is not a regular fixture object path"
+            excluded[digest] = record["excluded"]
+            continue
+        try:
+            raw = path.read_bytes()
+        except FileNotFoundError:
+            record["missing"] = "referenced original CAS bytes absent; no replacement sealed"
+            continue
+        record.update({
+            "actual_bytes": len(raw), "sha256": sha256(raw),
+            "length_matches": len(raw) == reference["bytes"],
+            "blake3_recomputed": False,
+        })
+        try:
+            value = json.loads(raw)
+        except (json.JSONDecodeError, UnicodeDecodeError):
+            value = None
+        if field := secret_field(value):
+            record["excluded"] = f"credential-bearing field {field}; original not disclosed"
+            excluded[digest] = record["excluded"]
+            continue
+        if digest not in retained:
+            total += len(raw)
+            if len(retained) >= MAX_OBJECTS or total > MAX_BYTES:
+                raise ValueError("fixture CAS retention budget exceeded")
+            retained[digest] = raw

+//! Real Cargo output, a stale default-target binary, and retained observations.
+//! These are compiler/receipt journeys, not a Shenko self-development acceptance.
+
+use anyhow::{Context, Result};
+
+use super::*;
+
+struct Workspace(PathBuf);
+
+impl Workspace {
+    fn new() -> Result<Self> {
+        let path = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("shenko-build-receipt-{}", EntityId::new()));
+        std::fs::create_dir_all(&path)?;
+        Ok(Self(path))
+    }
+}
+
+impl Drop for Workspace {
+    fn drop(&mut self) { let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&self.0); }
+}
+
+fn cargo() -> PathBuf {
+    std::env::var_os("CARGO").map(PathBuf::from).unwrap_or_else(|| PathBuf::from("cargo"))
+}
+
+fn project(path: &Path, package: &str, message: &str) -> Result<()> {
+    std::fs::create_dir_all(path.join("src"))?;
+    std::fs::write(path.join("Cargo.toml"), format!(
+        "[package]\nname = \"{package}\"\nversion = \"0.1.0\"\nedition = \"2024\"\n[[bin]]\nname = \"shenko\"\npath = \"src/main.rs\"\n"))?;
+    std::fs::write(path.join("src/main.rs"), format!("fn main() {{ println!(\"{message}\"); }}\n"))?;
+    Ok(())
+}
+
+fn request(path: &Path, generation: &str) -> BuildRequest {
+    let mut request = BuildRequest::new(path, RuntimeGeneration::new(generation));
+    request.profile = BuildProfile::Debug;
+    request.extra_args = vec!["--offline".into(), "--jobs=1".into()];
+    request
+}
+
+fn provider(target: PathBuf) -> CargoBuildProvider {
+    CargoBuildProvider {
+        cargo: cargo(), target_dir: Some(target),
+        limits: BuildLimits { timeout_ms: 120_000, stream_bytes: 1024 * 1024 },
+    }
+}
+
+fn read_json(cas: &ContentStore, reference: &ObjectRef) -> Result<serde_json::Value> {
+    let bytes = cas.read_object(&reference.digest)?;
+    anyhow::ensure!(Digest::blake3(&bytes) == reference.digest && bytes.len() as u64 == reference.bytes);
+    Ok(serde_json::from_slice(&bytes)?)
+}
+
+fn read_stream(cas: &ContentStore, value: &serde_json::Value) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {
+    let reference: ObjectRef = serde_json::from_value(value["raw_ref"].clone())?;
+    let bytes = cas.read_object(&reference.digest)?;
+    anyhow::ensure!(Digest::blake3(&bytes) == reference.digest && bytes.len() as u64 == reference.bytes);
+    Ok(bytes)
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn redirected_cargo_rebuild_keeps_the_actual_artifact_and_failed_attempt() -> Result<()> {
+    tokio::runtime::Builder::new_current_thread().enable_all().build()?.block_on(async {
+        let workspace = Workspace::new()?;
+        let source = workspace.0.join("source");
+        project(&source, "receipt-candidate", "old candidate")?;
+        std::fs::write(source.join("Cargo.lock"), "version = 4\n[[package]]\nname = \"receipt-candidate\"\nversion = \"0.1.0\"\n")?;
+        let build_request = request(&source, "build-a");
+        let first = provider(source.join("target")).build(&build_request).await?;
+        let first_artifact = first.artifact.as_ref().context("first Cargo build has no artifact")?;
+        let first_owned_path = first_artifact.path.clone();
+        let old_path = source.join("target").join("debug")
+            .join(first_artifact.path.file_name().context("actual binary has no filename")?);
+        std::fs::create_dir_all(old_path.parent().context("default artifact parent missing")?)?;
+        std::fs::copy(&first_owned_path, &old_path)?;
+        let old_digest = first_artifact.digest.clone();
+        let first_run = observe_command(&old_path, &[], &source, None, &probe_limits()).await;
+        anyhow::ensure!(first_run.succeeded(), "old artifact did not execute: {first_run:?}");
+        anyhow::ensure!(first_run.stdout.bytes == b"old candidate\n");
+
+        // The old executable stays at the layout guessed by the original bug.
+        // Cargo's next invocation places a different actual program elsewhere.
+        project(&source, "receipt-candidate", "rebuilt candidate")?;
+        let target = workspace.0.join("actual-target");
+        let builder = provider(workspace.0.join("provider-root"));
+        let mut second_request = request(&source, "build-b");
+        second_request.extra_args.extend(["--target-dir".into(), target.to_string_lossy().into_owned()]);
+        let rebuilt = builder.build(&second_request).await?;
+        let artifact = rebuilt.artifact.as_ref().context("rebuild has no artifact")?;
+        anyhow::ensure!(artifact.path.starts_with(std::fs::canonicalize(&target)?));
+        anyhow::ensure!(artifact.path != old_path && artifact.digest != old_digest);
+        anyhow::ensure!(Digest::blake3(&std::fs::read(&old_path)?) == old_digest);
+        let reported = rebuilt.compiler_artifact.as_ref().context("compiler evidence missing")?["executable"]
+            .as_str().context("reported executable missing")?;
+        anyhow::ensure!(std::fs::canonicalize(reported)? == artifact.path);
+        let layout = rebuilt.output_layout.as_ref().context("owned output identity missing")?;
+        anyhow::ensure!(layout.argument_root_preference.as_ref() == Some(&target));
+        let build_id = rebuilt.build_id.to_string();
+        anyhow::ensure!(layout.owned_directory.file_name().and_then(|name| name.to_str()) == Some(build_id.as_str()));
+        anyhow::ensure!(artifact.path.starts_with(&layout.owned_directory));
+        anyhow::ensure!(layout.owned_directory != first.output_layout.as_ref().context("first output identity missing")?.owned_directory);
+        anyhow::ensure!(Digest::blake3(&std::fs::read(&first_owned_path)?) == old_digest);
+        let execution = observe_command(&artifact.path, &[], &source, None, &probe_limits()).await;
+        anyhow::ensure!(execution.succeeded(), "rebuilt artifact did not execute: {execution:?}");
+        anyhow::ensure!(execution.stdout.bytes == b"rebuilt candidate\n");
+        anyhow::ensure!(artifact.source_revision.is_none(), "a non-checkout cannot claim a source commit");
+
+        let cas_dir = workspace.0.join("cas");
+        let cas = ContentStore::new(cas_dir.clone())?;
+        let receipt = rebuilt.seal(&cas)?;
+        drop(cas);
+        let reopened = ContentStore::open_existing(cas_dir.clone())?;
+        let saved = read_json(&reopened, &receipt)?;
+        let invocation = rebuilt.invocation.as_ref().context("original invocation missing")?;
+        anyhow::ensure!(read_stream(&reopened, &saved["invocation"]["stdout"])? == invocation.stdout.bytes);
+        anyhow::ensure!(read_stream(&reopened, &saved["invocation"]["stderr"])? == invocation.stderr.bytes);
+        anyhow::ensure!(saved["source_snapshot_frozen"] == false && saved["reproducible_build_proven"] == false);
+        anyhow::ensure!(saved["validation_tests_executed_by_builder"] == false);
+
+        // A later real compilation error retains its own failed invocation;
+        // neither of the two existing executables can be substituted for it.
+        std::fs::write(source.join("src/main.rs"), "fn main() { this is not Rust; }\n")?;
+        let failure = builder.build(&request(&source, "build-c")).await.err().context("invalid Rust unexpectedly built")?;
+        let failed = failure.outcome().context("failed invocation was discarded")?;
+        anyhow::ensure!(failed.artifact.is_none() && failed.build_id != rebuilt.build_id);
+        let failed_invocation = failed.invocation.as_ref().context("failed command missing")?;
+        anyhow::ensure!(failed_invocation.local_process_reaped && failed_invocation.stdout.eof && failed_invocation.stderr.eof);
+        anyhow::ensure!(failed_invocation.exit_code.is_some_and(|code| code != 0));
+        anyhow::ensure!(!failed_invocation.stdout.bytes.is_empty());
+        let failed_ref = failed.seal(&reopened)?;
+        drop(reopened);
+        let reopened = ContentStore::open_existing(cas_dir)?;
+        let failed_saved = read_json(&reopened, &failed_ref)?;
+        anyhow::ensure!(read_stream(&reopened, &failed_saved["invocation"]["stdout"])? == failed_invocation.stdout.bytes);
+        anyhow::ensure!(read_stream(&reopened, &failed_saved["invocation"]["stderr"])? == failed_invocation.stderr.bytes);
+        anyhow::ensure!(failed_saved["artifact"].is_null() && failed_saved["refusal"].is_string());
+        anyhow::ensure!(Digest::blake3(&std::fs::read(&artifact.path)?) == artifact.digest);
+        Ok(())
+    })
+}

+#[test]
+fn two_real_matching_cargo_targets_are_refused_as_ambiguous() -> Result<()> {
+    tokio::runtime::Builder::new_current_thread().enable_all().build()?.block_on(async {
+        let workspace = Workspace::new()?;
+        project(&workspace.0.join("a"), "candidate-a", "candidate a")?;
+        project(&workspace.0.join("b"), "candidate-b", "candidate b")?;
+        std::fs::write(workspace.0.join("Cargo.toml"), "[workspace]\nmembers = [\"a\", \"b\"]\nresolver = \"3\"\n")?;
+        std::fs::write(workspace.0.join("Cargo.lock"), "version = 4\n[[package]]\nname = \"candidate-a\"\nversion = \"0.1.0\"\n[[package]]\nname = \"candidate-b\"\nversion = \"0.1.0\"\n")?;
+        let error = provider(workspace.0.join("target")).build(&request(&workspace.0, "ambiguous")).await
+            .err().context("two matching binary targets were accepted")?;
+        let observed = error.outcome().context("ambiguous invocation was discarded")?;
+        anyhow::ensure!(observed.artifact.is_none());
+        anyhow::ensure!(observed.refusal.as_deref() == Some("multiple matching compiler artifacts are ambiguous"), "{error}");
+        let invocation = observed.invocation.as_ref().context("original command missing")?;
+        anyhow::ensure!(invocation.succeeded(), "expected real Cargo success before selection refusal: {invocation:?}");
+        let messages = invocation.stdout.bytes.split(|byte| *byte == b'\n')
+            .filter_map(|line| serde_json::from_slice::<serde_json::Value>(line).ok())
+            .filter(|message| message["reason"] == "compiler-artifact" && message["target"]["name"] == "shenko")
+            .count();
+        anyhow::ensure!(messages == 2, "actual matching compiler messages: {messages}");
+        Ok(())
+    })
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn overflowing_real_compiler_output_is_stopped_and_never_an_artifact() -> Result<()> {
+    tokio::runtime::Builder::new_current_thread().enable_all().build()?.block_on(async {
+        let workspace = Workspace::new()?;
+        project(&workspace.0, "bounded-candidate", "candidate")?;
+        std::fs::write(workspace.0.join("Cargo.lock"), "version = 4\n[[package]]\nname = \"bounded-candidate\"\nversion = \"0.1.0\"\n")?;
+        let mut builder = provider(workspace.0.join("target"));
+        builder.limits.stream_bytes = 16;
+        let error = builder.build(&request(&workspace.0, "bounded")).await
+            .err().context("truncated Cargo evidence was accepted")?;
+        let observed = error.outcome().context("overflow lost the original build attempt")?;
+        anyhow::ensure!(observed.artifact.is_none());
+        let invocation = observed.invocation.as_ref().context("overflow invocation missing")?;
+        anyhow::ensure!(invocation.stdout.truncated || invocation.stderr.truncated);
+        anyhow::ensure!(invocation.stdout.bytes.len() <= 16 && invocation.stderr.bytes.len() <= 16);
+        anyhow::ensure!(invocation.local_process_reaped && invocation.stdout.eof && invocation.stderr.eof,
+            "the original child and readers were not settled: {invocation:?}");
+        anyhow::ensure!(invocation.error.is_some() && invocation.cleanup_error.is_none(), "{invocation:?}");
+        Ok(())
+    })
+}"},{"sha":"11e359eb2d0d0d416f74a39cd54ed5f8a7ad79b5","filename":"docs/evidence/ci-3e62c0e5-20261116/source-blobs/11e359eb2d0d0d416f74a39cd54ed5f8a7ad79b5.blob","status":"added","additions":327,"deletions":0,"changes":327,"blob_url":"https://github.com/cyjin-yl/shenko/blob/41d785ae8f968a3e81cd632223cadb356c44a224/docs%2Fevidence%2Fci-3e62c0e5-20261116%2Fsource-blobs%2F11e359eb2d0d0d416f74a39cd54ed5f8a7ad79b5.blob","raw_url":"https://github.com/cyjin-yl/shenko/raw/41d785ae8f968a3e81cd632223cadb356c44a224/docs%2Fevidence%2Fci-3e62c0e5-20261116%2Fsource-blobs%2F11e359eb2d0d0d416f74a39cd54ed5f8a7ad79b5.blob","contents_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/cyjin-yl/shenko/contents/docs%2Fevidence%2Fci-3e62c0e5-20261116%2Fsource-blobs%2F11e359eb2d0d0d416f74a39cd54ed5f8a7ad79b5.blob?ref=41d785ae8f968a3e81cd632223cadb356c44a224","patch":"@@ -0,0 +1,327 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Compare real same-tool workspace diagnostics with an immutable PR baseline.
+
+Production and all-target diagnostics have separate per-package/per-lint counts.
+No checked-in warning budget is used. The same compiler enumerates its default
+Rust warnings for the workspace edition and probes which it actually accepts.
+Force-warn keeps these and Clippy's selected lints visible through allow/expect
+attributes. Unwrap/expect counts come only from normal library/binary builds,
+where rustc excludes test code; their complete all-target output is retained.
+The source-policy comparison rejects new suppressions, ignored tests and lint
+changes in either scope.
+"""
+import argparse
+from collections import Counter
+import json
+import os
+from pathlib import Path
+import re
+import subprocess
+import tomllib
+
+from base_ref import ROOT, resolve_base
+
+TOOLCHAIN = tomllib.loads((ROOT / 'rust-toolchain.toml').read_text())['toolchain']['channel']
+EDITION = tomllib.loads((ROOT / 'Cargo.toml').read_text())['workspace']['package']['edition']
+CLIPPY_LINTS = ('clippy::all', 'clippy::unwrap_used', 'clippy::expect_used')
+PRODUCTION_ONLY_LINTS = frozenset(CLIPPY_LINTS[1:])
+
+
+def lint_policy(output):
+    # Bind discovery and both source graphs to one native compiler. Inherited
+    # flags or wrappers must not replace that compiler or suppress its lints.
+    environment = dict(os.environ, RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=TOOLCHAIN)
+    for key in ('RUSTFLAGS', 'CARGO_ENCODED_RUSTFLAGS', 'CLIPPY_ARGS',
+                'RUSTC_WRAPPER', 'RUSTC_WORKSPACE_WRAPPER', 'RUSTC_BOOTSTRAP'):
+        environment.pop(key, None)
+    rustc = subprocess.check_output(
+        ['rustup', 'which', '--toolchain', TOOLCHAIN, 'rustc'], cwd=ROOT, env=environment, text=True).strip()
+    environment['RUSTC'] = rustc
+    command = [rustc, '--edition', EDITION, '-W', 'help']
+    listing = subprocess.check_output(command, cwd=ROOT, env=environment, text=True)
+    listing_path = output / 'rustc-lints.log'
+    listing_path.write_text(listing)
+    _, start, table = listing.partition('Lint checks provided by rustc:\n')
+    table, end, _ = table.partition('\nLint groups provided by rustc:')
+    rows = [line.split(None, 2) for line in table.splitlines() if line.strip()]
+    if not start or not end or rows[:2] != [['name', 'default', 'meaning'], ['----', '-------', '-------']]:
+        raise RuntimeError(f'Unrecognized rustc lint table; retained {listing_path}')
+    levels = {}
+    for row in rows[2:]:
+        if (len(row) != 3 or not re.fullmatch(r'[a-z][a-z0-9-]*', row[0])
+                or row[1] not in ('allow', 'expect', 'warn', 'force-warn', 'deny', 'forbid')
+                or row[0] in levels):
+            raise RuntimeError(f'Unrecognized rustc lint row {row!r}; retained {listing_path}')
+        levels[row[0]] = row[1]
+    # The special `warnings` group cannot be force-warned. Enumerate individual
+    # warn-by-default IDs instead: plain -W warnings permits source-level allow.
+    # Use this edition's defaults so deny-by-default lints are not downgraded.
+    warnings = sorted(name for name, level in levels.items() if level == 'warn' and name != 'warnings')
+    if not warnings:
+        raise RuntimeError(f'No default Rust warning lints discovered; retained {listing_path}')
+    warnings, probe = accepted_warning_lints(rustc, environment, output, warnings)
+    flags = [argument for name in (*warnings, *CLIPPY_LINTS) for argument in ('--force-warn', name)]
+    policy = {
+        'toolchain': TOOLCHAIN, 'edition': EDITION, 'rustc_path': rustc,
+        'rustc': subprocess.check_output([rustc, '-Vv'], cwd=ROOT, env=environment, text=True),
+        'clippy': subprocess.check_output(
+            ['cargo', 'clippy', '--version'], cwd=ROOT, env=environment, text=True).strip(),
+        'lint_discovery_command': command, 'rust_warning_probe': probe,
+        'rust_warning_lints': warnings, 'flags': flags,
+    }
+    # Retain the shared policy even if the first compilation fails.
+    (output / 'lint-policy.json').write_text(json.dumps(policy, indent=2) + '\n')
+    return environment, policy
+
+
+def accepted_warning_lints(rustc, environment, output, discovered):
+    """Check the listing against the exact compiler's command-line interface.
+
+    Stable rustc may list an unstable lint in -W help, then reject that lint's
+    name when it appears in --force-warn. That creates unknown_lints in every
+    crate, including otherwise clean new crates. Only names this compiler
+    itself rejects in an isolated probe are omitted; source diagnostics and
+    the unknown_lints lint remain part of both workspace comparisons.
+    """
+    source = output / 'rustc-warning-probe.rs'
+    source.write_text('pub fn clippy_ratchet_probe() {}\n')
+    discovered = set(discovered)
+    if 'unknown-lints' not in discovered:
+        raise RuntimeError('Compiler discovery did not include unknown-lints')
+
+    def probe(names, stage):
+        command = [rustc, '--edition', EDITION, '--crate-name', 'shenko_lint_policy_probe',
+                   '--crate-type', 'lib', '--emit', 'metadata', '--error-format', 'json',
+                   *[argument for name in sorted(names) for argument in ('--force-warn', name)],
+                   '-o', str(output / f'rustc-warning-probe-{stage}.rmeta'), str(source)]
+        result = subprocess.run(command, cwd=ROOT, env=environment, text=True,
+                                stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, timeout=30)
+        diagnostics_path = output / f'rustc-warning-probe-{stage}.jsonl'
+        diagnostics_path.write_text(result.stderr)
+        (output / f'rustc-warning-probe-{stage}.stdout.log').write_text(result.stdout)
+        receipt = {'command': command, 'returncode': result.returncode,
+                   'diagnostics': diagnostics_path.name, 'source': source.read_text()}
+        (output / f'rustc-warning-probe-{stage}.json').write_text(json.dumps(receipt, indent=2) + '\n')
+        if result.returncode or result.stdout:
+            raise RuntimeError(f'rustc lint probe failed; retained {diagnostics_path}')
+        rejected = set()
+        warnings = 0
+        summaries = []
+        for line in result.stderr.splitlines():
+            diagnostic = json.loads(line)
+            code = (diagnostic.get('code') or {}).get('code')
+            message = diagnostic.get('message', '')
+            unknown = re.fullmatch(r'unknown lint: `([a-z][a-z0-9_-]*)`', message)
+            summary = re.fullmatch(r'(\d+) warnings? emitted', message)
+            if (diagnostic.get('$message_type') != 'diagnostic'
+                    or diagnostic.get('level') != 'warning'):
+                raise RuntimeError(f'Unexpected rustc probe diagnostic; retained {diagnostics_path}')
+            if code == 'unknown_lints' and unknown:
+                name = unknown[1].replace('_', '-')
+                if name not in names or name == 'unknown-lints':
+                    raise RuntimeError(f'Unexpected rejected lint {name!r}; retained {diagnostics_path}')
+                rejected.add(name)
+                warnings += 1
+            elif code is None and summary:
+                summaries.append(int(summary[1]))
+            else:
+                raise RuntimeError(f'Unexpected rustc probe warning; retained {diagnostics_path}')
+        if summaries != ([warnings] if warnings else []):
+            raise RuntimeError(f'Inconsistent rustc probe warning count; retained {diagnostics_path}')
+        return rejected, receipt
+
+    rejected, initial = probe(discovered, 'discovered')
+    accepted = sorted(discovered - rejected)
+    remaining, verified = probe(accepted, 'accepted')
+    if remaining:
+        raise RuntimeError(f'Compiler still rejects filtered lint policy: {sorted(remaining)}')
+    return accepted, {'discovered_lints': sorted(discovered), 'unavailable_lints': sorted(rejected),
+                      'initial': initial, 'verified': verified}
+
+
+def tracked(root):
+    return subprocess.check_output(['git', 'ls-files', '-z'], cwd=root).decode().split('\0')[:-1]
+
+
+def rust_tokens(source):
+    """Read attributes without mistaking strings or nested comments for code."""
+    index = 0
+    while index < len(source):
+        if source[index].isspace():
+            index += 1
+        elif source.startswith('//', index):
+            end = source.find('\n', index)
+            index = len(source) if end < 0 else end + 1
+        elif source.startswith('/*', index):
+            depth = 1
+            index += 2
+            while depth:
+                if index >= len(source):
+                    raise ValueError('Unterminated Rust block comment')
+                if source.startswith('/*', index):
+                    depth += 1
+                    index += 2
+                elif source.startswith('*/', index):
+                    depth -= 1
+                    index += 2
+                else:
+                    index += 1
+        else:
+            raw = re.match(r'(?:br|cr|r)(#*)"', source[index:])
+            if raw:
+                end = source.find('"' + raw[1], index + raw.end())
+                if end < 0:
+                    raise ValueError('Unterminated Rust raw string')
+                end += 1 + len(raw[1])
+            elif source[index] == '"':
+                end = index + 1
+                while end < len(source) and source[end] != '"':
+                    end += 2 if source[end] == '\\' else 1
+                end += 1
+            else:
+                character = re.match(r"'(?:\\(?:u\{[0-9a-fA-F_]+\}|x[0-9a-fA-F]{2}|.)|[^'\\\n])'", source[index:])
+                word = re.match(r'[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*', source[index:])
+                end = index + (character.end() if character else word.end() if word else 1)
+            yield source[index:end]
+            index = end
+
+
+def source_policy(root):
+    controls = Counter()
+    configuration = {}
+    for name in tracked(root):
+        path = root / name
+        if name.endswith('.rs'):
+            tokens = list(rust_tokens(path.read_text()))
+            index = 0
+            while index < len(tokens):
+                if tokens[index] != '#':
+                    index += 1
+                    continue
+                start = index
+                index += 1
+                if index < len(tokens) and tokens[index] == '!':
+                    index += 1
+                if index >= len(tokens) or tokens[index] != '[':
+                    continue
+                depth = 1
+                index += 1
+                while depth and index < len(tokens):
+                    depth += (tokens[index] == '[') - (tokens[index] == ']')
+                    index += 1
+                attribute = tokens[start:index]
+                if {'allow', 'expect', 'ignore'} & set(attribute):
+                    controls[(name, ' '.join(attribute))] += 1
+        elif path.name == 'Cargo.toml':
+            manifest = tomllib.loads(path.read_text())
+            for section, table in [('lints', manifest.get('lints', {})),
+                                   ('workspace.lints', manifest.get('workspace', {}).get('lints', {}))]:
+                for tool, entries in table.items():
+                    if not isinstance(entries, dict):
+                        continue
+                    for lint, value in entries.items():
+                        level = value.get('level') if isinstance(value, dict) else value
+                        if level in ('allow', 'expect'):
+                            controls[(name, f'{section}.{tool}.{lint}={json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True)}')] += 1
+        elif path.name in ('clippy.toml', '.clippy.toml') or name.endswith(('.cargo/config', '.cargo/config.toml')):
+            configuration[name] = path.read_bytes()
+    return controls, configuration
+
+
+def collect(root, target, output, selection, environment, lint_flags, *, production):
+    environment = dict(environment, CARGO_TARGET_DIR=str(target))
+    metadata = json.loads(subprocess.check_output(
+        ['cargo', 'metadata', '--locked', '--no-deps', '--format-version=1'], cwd=root, env=environment, text=True))
+    members = set(metadata['workspace_members'])
+    packages = {package['id']: package['name'] for package in metadata['packages'] if package['id'] in members}
+    # Match the Rust job's optional Poppy assembly in both immutable trees.
+    # Building the protocol workspace member alone does not compile the bin's
+    # feature-gated account, transport and commerce handlers.
+    command = ['cargo', 'clippy', '--workspace', '--features', 'shenko/compat-poppy',
+               '--locked', '-j2', '--message-format=json', *selection, '--', *lint_flags]
+    counts = Counter()
+    production_only = Counter()
+    artifacts = set()
+    finished = False
+    print(f'{root}: {" ".join(command)}', flush=True)
+    with output.with_suffix('.jsonl').open('w') as log, output.with_suffix('.stderr.log').open('w') as errors:
+        process = subprocess.Popen(command, cwd=root, env=environment, text=True, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=errors)
+        for line in process.stdout:
+            log.write(line)
+            log.flush()
+            record = json.loads(line)
+            if record.get('reason') == 'build-finished':
+                finished = record['success']
+            if record.get('package_id') not in packages:
+                continue
+            if record.get('reason') == 'compiler-artifact':
+                artifacts.add(packages[record['package_id']])
+            if record.get('reason') == 'compiler-message':
+                diagnostic = record['message']
+                if diagnostic['level'] in ('warning', 'error'):
+                    print(diagnostic.get('rendered') or diagnostic['message'], flush=True)
+                if diagnostic['level'] == 'warning':
+                    code = (diagnostic.get('code') or {}).get('code') or diagnostic['message']
+                    key = (packages[record['package_id']], code)
+                    if code in PRODUCTION_ONLY_LINTS and not production:
+                        production_only[key] += 1
+                    else:
+                        counts[key] += 1
+        status = process.wait()
+    if status or not finished or not artifacts:
+        raise RuntimeError(f'Clippy failed ({status}) in {root}; retained {output.with_suffix(".stderr.log")}')
+    return counts, production_only
+
+
+def diagnostic_counts(counts):
+    return [{'package': key[0], 'lint': key[1], 'count': count}
+            for key, count in sorted(counts.items())]
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument('--base', required=True)
+    parser.add_argument('--output', type=Path, default=ROOT / '.ci/evidence/clippy')
+    parser.add_argument('--target-root', type=Path, default=ROOT / '.ci/target/clippy')
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    base = resolve_base(args.base)
+    output = args.output.resolve()
+    output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
+    environment, policy = lint_policy(output)
+    baseline = output / 'baseline'
+    subprocess.run(['git', 'worktree', 'add', '--detach', str(baseline), base], cwd=ROOT, check=True)
+    base_controls, base_configuration = source_policy(baseline)
+    current_controls, current_configuration = source_policy(ROOT)
+    errors = [f'New suppression/ignored test: {name}: {attribute}'
+              for name, attribute in sorted((current_controls - base_controls).elements())]
+    if base_configuration != current_configuration:
+        errors.append('Clippy/Cargo configuration differs from the immutable baseline; lint policy cannot lower its own gate')
+    comparisons = {}
+    for scope, selection in [('production', ['--lib', '--bins']), ('all-targets', ['--all-targets'])]:
+        old, old_production_only = collect(
+            baseline, args.target_root.resolve() / 'baseline' / scope, output / f'base-{scope}', selection,
+            environment, policy['flags'], production=scope == 'production')
+        new, new_production_only = collect(
+            ROOT, args.target_root.resolve() / 'candidate' / scope, output / f'candidate-{scope}', selection,
+            environment, policy['flags'], production=scope == 'production')
+        comparisons[scope] = {
+            'cargo_target_selection': selection,
+            'production_only_lints_compared': scope == 'production',
+            'baseline': diagnostic_counts(old), 'candidate': diagnostic_counts(new),
+            'baseline_uncompared_production_only_diagnostics': diagnostic_counts(old_production_only),
+            'candidate_uncompared_production_only_diagnostics': diagnostic_counts(new_production_only),
+        }
+        errors.extend(f'{scope}: {package}: {lint} increased by {count}'
+                      for (package, lint), count in sorted((new - old).items()))
+    receipt = {'baseline': base, 'candidate': subprocess.check_output(
+        ['git', 'rev-parse', 'HEAD'], cwd=ROOT, text=True).strip(),
+        **policy, 'comparisons': comparisons, 'errors': errors}
+    receipt['production_only_lints'] = sorted(PRODUCTION_ONLY_LINTS)
+    (output / 'ratchet.json').write_text(json.dumps(receipt, indent=2) + '\n')
+    if errors:
+        raise SystemExit('\n'.join(errors))
+    print('Compiler/Clippy warnings and production unwrap/expect diagnostics do not exceed the immutable baseline')
+

+name: CI
+
+on:

+    types: [opened, reopened, synchronize, ready_for_review, edited]
+  merge_group:

+  push:
+    branches: [main]
+  workflow_dispatch:
+    inputs:
+      base-sha:
+        description: Full independently reviewed ancestor SHA for the ratchets

+        type: string

+permissions:
+  contents: read

+concurrency:
+  group: ci-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
+  cancel-in-progress: true
+
+defaults:
+  run:
+    shell: bash --noprofile --norc -e -o pipefail {0}

+env:

+  CARGO_INCREMENTAL: '0'
+  CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG: '0'
+  CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG: '0'

+jobs:
+  rust:

+    container: rust:1.98.1-bookworm

+    env:
+      CARGO_TARGET_DIR: ${{ github.workspace }}/.ci/target/rust
+      SHENKO_COMPAT_EVIDENCE_ROOT: ${{ github.workspace }}/.ci/evidence/compat
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+        with:
+          fetch-depth: 0
+          persist-credentials: false
+      # Checkout writes safe.directory under a temporary HOME. After each
+      # checkout, register only the runtime workspace in the restored shell

+      - name: Trust the checked-out workspace in the container shell

+      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
+        with:
+          workspaces: . -> .ci/target/rust

+          mkdir -p .ci/evidence

+          echo 'b761e3a0721dbae9c09a0059e5fdb2bf917d1b4a8a7b430fb3b5aafb0984b2c4  .ci/toolchains/wasi-sdk.tar.gz' | sha256sum --check --strict

+          python3 crates/shenko-wasm/ports/ssh-wasi/build.py \

+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

+    steps:

+//! Checkout metadata is an observation, not an immutable source snapshot.

+use std::process::Stdio;

+const OUTPUT_TAIL_BYTES: usize = 8 * 1024;

+#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]

+#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
+pub struct BuildRequest {

+}
+
+impl BuildRequest {
+    pub fn new(source_dir: impl Into<PathBuf>, generation: RuntimeGeneration) -> Self {
+        Self {
+            source_dir: source_dir.into(), generation, profile: BuildProfile::Release,
+            target: None, extra_args: Vec::new(), binary_name: "shenko".into(),

+/// Finite collection limits of this build provider, recorded in each attempt.
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
+pub struct BuildLimits {

+    pub stream_bytes: usize,
+}
+
+impl Default for BuildLimits {

+#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
+pub struct CandidateArtifact {
+    pub generation: RuntimeGeneration,
+    pub path: PathBuf,
+    pub digest: Digest,
+    pub bytes: u64,
+    /// Equal, clean checkout HEAD observations before and after this build.
+    /// Even this does not attest ignored files, environment or immutable inputs.
+    pub source_revision: Option<String>,
+    pub lockfile_digest: Option<Digest>,
+    pub manifest_digest: Option<Digest>,
+    /// Cargo's observed version in the build directory, not a compiler attestation.
+    pub toolchain: String,
+    /// The requested profile and target; the receipt also retains Cargo's actual
+    /// compiler profile and exact arguments, including additional arguments.
+    pub profile: BuildProfile,
+    pub target: Option<String>,
+    pub built_at: String,
+}

+/// Exact retained bytes. Overflow is a failed observation, never a valid build
+/// whose compiler messages were silently discarded.
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, Serialize, Deserialize)]
+pub struct CapturedStream {
+    pub bytes: Vec<u8>,
+    pub observed_bytes: u64,
+    pub eof: bool,
+    pub truncated: bool,
+    pub error: Option<String>,
+}
+
+impl CapturedStream {
+    fn append(&mut self, bytes: &[u8], limit: usize) {
+        self.observed_bytes = self.observed_bytes.saturating_add(bytes.len() as u64);
+        let retained = limit.saturating_sub(self.bytes.len()).min(bytes.len());
+        self.bytes.extend_from_slice(&bytes[..retained]);
+        self.truncated |= retained != bytes.len();
+    }
+
+    fn complete(&self) -> bool { self.eof && !self.truncated && self.error.is_none() }
+
+    fn seal(&self, cas: &ContentStore, name: &str) -> anyhow::Result<serde_json::Value> {
+        let object = cas.seal_object(&self.bytes, "application/octet-stream", "activation", name, 1)?.object;
+        Ok(serde_json::json!({
+            "raw_ref": object, "observed_bytes": self.observed_bytes,
+            "eof": self.eof, "truncated": self.truncated, "error": self.error,
+        }))
+    }
+}

+#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
+pub struct CommandObservation {
+    pub command: Vec<String>,
+    pub cwd: PathBuf,
+    pub explicit_target_dir: Option<PathBuf>,
+    pub limits: BuildLimits,
+    pub started_at: String,
+    pub finished_at: String,
+    pub pid: Option<u32>,
+    pub exit_code: Option<i32>,
+    pub local_process_reaped: bool,
+    pub stdout: CapturedStream,
+    pub stderr: CapturedStream,
+    pub error: Option<String>,
+    pub cleanup_error: Option<String>,
+}
+
+impl CommandObservation {
+    fn succeeded(&self) -> bool {
+        self.exit_code == Some(0) && self.local_process_reaped && self.error.is_none()
+            && self.cleanup_error.is_none() && self.stdout.complete() && self.stderr.complete()
+    }
+
+    fn seal(&self, cas: &ContentStore) -> anyhow::Result<serde_json::Value> {
+        Ok(serde_json::json!({
+            "command": self.command, "cwd": self.cwd, "explicit_target_dir": self.explicit_target_dir,
+            "limits": self.limits, "started_at": self.started_at, "finished_at": self.finished_at,
+            "pid": self.pid, "exit_code": self.exit_code, "local_process_reaped": self.local_process_reaped,
+            "stdout": self.stdout.seal(cas, "build-stdout")?,
+            "stderr": self.stderr.seal(cas, "build-stderr")?,
+            "error": self.error, "cleanup_error": self.cleanup_error,
+        }))
+    }
+}
